signals.topic: Qwen qwen3-coder-plus model returns 400 Bad Request — model unusable after recent regression
signals.summary: The qwen3-coder-plus model with the qwen-code provider returns 400 invalid_parameter_error on every request (including simple prompts), across both VS Code and JetBrains IDEs. This is reported as a regression — it previously worked. Root cause appears related to streaming parameter handling in the qwen-code provider.
signals.review_reason: count=2 confirmed across two different IDE platforms (VS Code + JetBrains) with identical symptoms — a clear regression. The model fails 100% of requests, making it completely unusable. The count meets the P0 threshold. The 'previous stable + regression after updates' framing provides strong user impact evidence.

source_issues.title: Recent Regression — 400 Bad Request with qwen3-coder-plus
source_issues.evidence: Status 400, code invalid_parameter_error, modelId qwen3-coder-plus. Previously working, regression after recent updates. Fails on every request including 'Hello' prompts. Error screenshot attached.

source_issues.title: Error when trying to query Qwen
source_issues.evidence: Same 400 invalid_parameter_error for qwen3-coder-plus on qwen-code provider. Reproducible in both VS Code and Rider. Reporter notes the model cannot stream properly even when streaming is requested.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock: model stream repeatedly ends without output, hitting consecutive mistake limit and stopping session
signals.summary: When using AWS Bedrock as the API provider, the model stream consistently ends without producing output, triggering automatic retries that all fail, eventually hitting the 6 consecutive mistake limit and stopping the entire session. This blocks the primary use case of running tasks via Cline CLI with Bedrock.
aliases: Bedrock model stream ends without producing output
signals.review_reason: User confirms this blocks the primary workflow: every task fails with stream-end errors, retries all fail, and the session is abandoned after the mistake limit. While only 1 issue, the severity is high (complete workflow failure on a specific provider). The evidence of persistent, reproducible failure across multiple attempts in a single session meets the bar for a user pain point.

source_issues.title: Model stream repeatedly ends without producing output when using AWS Bedrock — hits consecutive mistake limit
source_issues.evidence: Model stream consistently fails with 'No output generated. Check the stream for errors.' Retries also fail. After 6 consecutive failures, session stops with 'Stopped after 6/6 consecutive mistakes (api_error)'. Persistent on almost every task/session.

signals.topic: Cline SDK agent.shutdown() blocks indefinitely in CLI environment
signals.summary: When using the official Cline SDK example in a Node.js CLI environment, calling agent.shutdown() causes the process to hang indefinitely, preventing any cleanup or exit.
signals.review_reason: Blocking the SDK's own documented usage path prevents developers from properly integrating or exiting from the SDK. While count=1 and single-repo, the indefinite hang is a complete workflow blocker for SDK users in CLI contexts. Not P0 only because the population of SDK CLI users is smaller and no other corroborating reports exist yet.

source_issues.title: Cline SDK: agent.shutdown() may block indefinitely in CLI usage
source_issues.evidence: Official SDK example from docs gets stuck at 'await agent.shutdown()' indefinitely in Node.js CLI environment. No workaround described. Screenshot attached showing process stuck.

signals.topic: OpenAI Compatible provider: token usage counter inflates to millions, thinking tags and tool calls render as raw unparsed text
signals.summary: When using OpenAI Compatible providers (e.g. NVIDIA, MiniMax), the context token usage bar in the UI shows astronomical inflated values (15M+ tokens) because the OpenAI handler yields usage chunks without deduplication. Additionally, raw <think> thinking tags and [TOOL_CALL] blocks are rendered as plain text in the UI instead of being parsed, making output unreadable.
aliases: usage counter resets to 0 on thinking steps
signals.review_reason: This is a clear UX defect with visible user impact: (1) inflated token counts mislead users about API usage and costs, (2) raw thinking tags and tool calls make output unreadable and non-functional. Multiple distinct symptoms from a single root cause (missing deduplication guard in OpenAiHandler). Screenshots provide concrete evidence. Not P0 as the core chat functionality remains usable, but the UX degradation is significant.

source_issues.title: OpenAI Compatible providers: token count inflates to 15M+, <think> tags render as plain text, and tool calls appear unparsed in UI
source_issues.evidence: Token count inflates to 15M+ because OpenAiHandler yields usage on every chunk.usage occurrence without dedup. Raw <think> and [TOOL_CALL] blocks render verbatim in UI. Screenshots attached showing 15M+ token display and raw markup in output. Root cause identified: missing didOutputUsage guard in openai.ts vs. correctly implemented in openrouter.ts.

signals.topic: JetBrains plugin: adding files or folders returns 'no results found' — core file-selection functionality broken
signals.summary: In recent versions of the CLine JetBrains plugin (tested on PHPstorm 2026.1 and 2025.3.4), clicking 'add files' or 'add folder' returns a 'no results found' message, making the plugin unusable since file selection is a fundamental prerequisite for any task.
aliases: no results found when adding files in PHPstorm
signals.review_reason: File/folder selection is a prerequisite step for any Cline task — when it returns 'no results found' every time, the entire JetBrains plugin workflow is blocked. The user explicitly labels the tool as 'unusable'. This is a main flow failure meeting the P0 threshold: core functionality completely unavailable, reproducible, and confirmed across multiple IDE versions.

source_issues.title: Cannot add files or folders in PHPstorm 2026.1
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states: 'this makes CLine unusable to me'. File/folder addition is broken in both PHPstorm 2026.1 and 2025.3.4. Reproducible 100% of the time.

signals.topic: Session file not created/loaded in IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate (Windows) — blocks all Continue usage in this IDE
signals.summary: On IntelliJ IDEA 2026.1 Ultimate edition (Windows), the Continue plugin fails to create session .json files on disk, causing "Session file does not exist" errors on every restart. The plugin works in Community Edition on the same machine. This completely blocks the core Continue workflow.
aliases: session persistence failure in JetBrains IDE
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：session 文件持久化失败导致 Continue 核心功能在 IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate (Windows) 上完全不可用。虽然只有1条，但错误场景清晰，用户已尝试多种排查手段（清缓存、重装IDE、验证权限），且该 IDE 组合（IU 2026.1 + Windows）有明确复现路径，属主流程阻断级痛点。

source_issues.title: Session file does not exist
source_issues.evidence: Error loading session: Error: Session file C:\Users\...\.continue\sessions\[ID].json does not exist. Plugin generates new session IDs on each restart but never writes the file. Verified on same machine Community Edition works, Ultimate does not. Tried clearing .continue, JetBrains config, reinstalling IDE — issue persists.

signals.topic: CLI install script checks wrong path for fnm binary, breaking macOS CLI installation
signals.summary: The install script checks `if [ ! -x "$FNM_INSTALL_DIR" ]` instead of `if [ ! -x "$FNM_INSTALL_DIR/fnm" ]`, causing it to fail even when fnm is correctly installed via Homebrew on macOS. Users cannot install the Continue CLI at all.
aliases: fnm binary not found installation error
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：安装脚本路径检查错误导致 CLI 在 macOS 上完全无法安装，阻断首次使用流程。根因明确（路径拼接缺失 /fnm 子路径），影响所有 macOS + Homebrew + fnm 用户。

source_issues.title: Install script is not working due fnm binary
source_issues.evidence: Error: fnm installation failed - binary not found at /Users/rgildein/.local/share/fnm/fnm. fnm 1.39.0 is already installed and up-to-date via Homebrew. Script checks `if [ ! -x "$FNM_INSTALL_DIR" ]` instead of `if [ ! -x "$FNM_INSTALL_DIR/fnm" ]`. Blocks CLI installation entirely on macOS.

signals.topic: "Headers is not defined" ReferenceError breaks LLM chat in code-server (Linux/Node environments)
signals.summary: When running the VS Code extension in code-server (Linux, Node.js environment), all LLM chat requests fail with `ReferenceError: Headers is not defined`. The `Headers` Web API is used in the OpenAI adapter without Node.js compatibility, completely blocking the core LLM chat workflow.
aliases: Headers is not defined in code-server
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Web API `Headers` 在 Node.js/code-server 环境中不存在，导致 OpenAI adapter 构建请求时直接抛出 ReferenceError，所有 LLM 对话完全不可用。用户明确表示该问题反复困扰多个用户，影响核心对话功能。

source_issues.title: "Headers not defined" -> This time with logs
source_issues.evidence: ReferenceError: Headers is not defined at buildHeaders in OpenAI.buildBody. Stack trace shows `out/extension.js:209433:29`. Issue is recurring ('has plagued me and other users'). A network request is never made to the server — the extension crashes before making any API call. Reproduced on code-server on Linux. Affects all LLM chat in this environment.

signals.topic: @file context length check incorrectly rejects files that fit within model's context window
signals.summary: Using @file to include a file in a chat prompt fails with "File exceeds model's context length", but opening the same file with @CurrentFile works fine. The Continue console confirms the same file content is within the token limit (14k tokens within 128k). The @file directive uses an incorrect file size / token estimation that over-restricts file inclusion.
signals.review_reason: 影响明显但非完全阻断：@file 是用户使用频率极高的核心上下文引用方式，其错误限制导致用户无法通过该指令引用中等大小的代码文件，显著影响核心使用体验和工作流效率。对比 @CurrentFile 的正确行为，根因明确。

source_issues.title: @file applies the wrong context lenght limit but @CurrentFile works fine.
source_issues.evidence: Files around 20kB (300 lines of Python) trigger false 'File exceeds model's context length' warning when using @file. The same file via @CurrentFile shows 14k tokens in the prompt, well within the 128k context window. @file directive incorrectly calculates context limit, blocking file-context workflow.

signals.topic: Add Model UI shows stale provider models after switching providers while a fetch is in flight
signals.summary: When a dynamic model fetch is in flight in the Add Model UI and the user switches to a different provider before the request resolves, the late-resolving request from the previous provider can populate the model list under the new provider. This leads to incorrect model selection and confusing UX.
aliases: Add Model async state race condition
wrong models shown after provider switch
signals.review_reason: 影响明显但非阻断：竞态条件导致添加模型时错误展示其他 provider 的模型列表，可能导致用户选错模型配置。非高频操作场景，但影响模型配置的核心设置流程。

source_issues.title: Add Model UI can show stale models from a previously selected provider after dynamic fetch resolves late
source_issues.evidence: Async closure captures stale `selectedProvider` at request time. User selects OpenAI, triggers fetch, switches to Anthropic before resolution, and OpenAI models still appear in the Anthropic list when the delayed request resolves. Reproduced deterministically in focused GUI test. Affects model selection in Add Model flow.

signals.topic: ChatWithCrewFlow init blocks on LLM call at module import, crashes containerized deployments
signals.summary: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ triggers synchronous blocking LLM calls at module import time. Any LLM provider hiccup (500/503, rate-limit, network blip, invalid credentials) crashes the Python process before uvicorn binds to its HTTP port, causing Railway/Kubernetes/AWS ECS/Fly.io deployments to fail and rollback.
aliases: LLM call at module import time
signals.review_reason: Complete process crash with no graceful fallback. All containerized deployment paths (Railway, Kubernetes, AWS ECS, Fly.io) are blocked on any transient LLM error. No timeout, retry, or opt-out mechanism exists, making it a P0 deployment blocker.

source_issues.title: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ makes blocking LLM call at module import, crashes containers on any LLM hiccup
source_issues.evidence: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ triggers synchronous blocking LLM calls at module import time via generate_crew_chat_inputs. ANY LLM provider hiccup (500/503, rate-limit, network blip, invalid credentials) causes the Python process to crash before uvicorn binds to its HTTP port. In orchestrated environments (Railway, Kubernetes, AWS ECS, Fly.io), the platform marks the deploy failed and rolls back. No timeout, retry, try/except, or opt-out available.

signals.topic: Checkpointing fails with Pydantic models and guardrail retry type mismatch
signals.summary: Two bugs: (1) Checkpointing fails with PydanticSerializationError when Flow state contains Pydantic models. (2) Guardrail retry fails with TaskOutput type mismatch when tasks use output_pydantic (passes Pydantic object where string expected).
aliases: Flow checkpoint restore broken with Pydantic
signals.review_reason: Two distinct failures breaking core Flow persistence (checkpoint/restore) and guardrail retry when Pydantic models are used. Affects any user who uses structured Pydantic output in Flows — a core feature.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Checkpointing + guardrail retry incompatible with Pydantic outputs in Flow
source_issues.evidence: Two bugs: (1) Checkpointing fails when Flow state contains Pydantic models with PydanticSerializationError: Unable to serialize unknown type: <class 'pydantic._internal._model_construction.ModelMetaclass'>. (2) Guardrail retry breaks when a task uses output_pydantic causing TaskOutput type mismatch during retry (passes Pydantic object where string is expected).

signals.topic: Multimodal input_files silently ignored when Crew.agents not explicitly provided
signals.summary: When Task.input_files is used with an agent-assigned Task, if Crew.agents is not explicitly provided the files are silently dropped. The task runs normally but the model receives no image, with no error or warning.
aliases: input_files not passed to task agent
signals.review_reason: Silent failure with no error or warning. The API design is misleading — task.agent should suffice per documentation but does not. Users lose multimodal capability with no indication of why.

source_issues.title: [BUG] CrewAI: Task.input_files + missing Crew.agents causes multimodal files to be ignored
source_issues.evidence: When using multimodal inputs (input_files) with a Task that has an agent assigned, if Crew.agents is not explicitly provided, the files are silently ignored. The task runs but the model behaves as if no image was provided. Contradicts expected API usage where task.agent should be sufficient. Silent failure makes debugging difficult.

signals.topic: OpenRouter thinking models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro) fail with ValueError in chained requests
signals.summary: Specific OpenRouter thinking-model variants (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5, anthropic/claude-opus-4-5, gemini-3.1-pro-preview) return empty responses causing ValueError during multi-agent chained requests, while other providers work correctly.
signals.review_reason: Specific model variants fail deterministically in multi-agent chained workflows while identical setup works for other providers. Blocks academic writing generation workflows that depend on these models.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Problems with OpenRouter thinking models
source_issues.evidence: When using OpenRouter APIs with models like anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5, anthropic/claude-opus-4-5, or gemini-3.1-pro-preview, errors occur during multi-agent chained requests for academic writing generation. Error: ValueError: Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty. Other models (GLM, Qwen, GPT) work fine under the same setup.

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock Anthropic V3 deprecated by AWS, V4 not supported in CrewAI — Anthropic models completely unavailable on Bedrock
signals.summary: AWS has deprecated Bedrock's Anthropic V3 models (only legacy access). Anthropic V4 is not available in CrewAI. Existing AWS Bedrock users are fully blocked from using Anthropic models in CrewAI.
aliases: Bedrock V3 deprecated no V4 support
signals.review_reason: Key feature completely unavailable for AWS Bedrock users. AWS has deprecated V3 and CrewAI lacks V4 support, leaving users with no Anthropic model option on Bedrock — a significant platform gap.

source_issues.title: [FEATURE] Anthropic V4 support in Bedrock LLM's
source_issues.evidence: Bedrock's Anthropic V3 models are no longer available at AWS (only for legacy customers). V4 models are not available in CrewAI. Existing AWS Bedrock users are blocked from using Anthropic models in CrewAI.

signals.topic: /chat SSE endpoint emits 'complete' event on strategy loading failure instead of 'error' event, causing silent client-side misclassification of failures
signals.summary: SSE endpoint violates its own streaming contract by emitting 'complete' with empty content when request assembly fails (e.g., invalid strategy name), misleading clients into treating failed requests as successful.
signals.review_reason: This violates the SSE streaming contract: the endpoint signals success ('complete') for a failed request. Clients relying on 'complete' as a success signal will silently misclassify failures. While count=1, the impact is systemic for any SSE client integration — all API consumers of /chat are affected by this contract violation.

source_issues.title: /chat SSE returns complete even when strategy loading fails
source_issues.evidence: The SSE endpoint emits 'complete' event with empty content instead of 'error' when prompt/session construction fails, causing clients to misclassify failed requests as successful. Handler logs internal error but still closes stream normally.

signals.topic: YouTube visual OCR output uses index-based timestamps instead of actual frame timestamps, producing misleading temporal references
signals.summary: GrabVisual() computes frame timestamps from result index (i.e., nth frame labeled as second n) rather than using the actual ffmpeg-reported frame time, causing OCR text to be attributed to wrong moments in the source video.
signals.review_reason: This is a data accuracy defect in YouTube visual extraction: timestamps are systematically wrong while appearing precise. Downstream users or prompts that rely on these timestamps to correlate OCR text with video moments will get incorrect associations. Not P0 because it does not block the tool from running — only reduces output reliability.

source_issues.title: YouTube visual OCR output uses index-based timestamps instead of real frame timing
source_issues.evidence: GrabVisual() uses 'secs := i' (frame index) for timestamp rendering instead of actual ffmpeg-reported frame time. OCR text is incorrectly attributed to wrong video moments, reducing output trustworthiness and misleading downstream processing.

signals.topic: Codex provider returns empty response, breaking the core summarize/pattern workflow for affected users
signals.summary: When using the Codex provider (authenticated at chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex), fabric returns 'empty response' to the user, failing the primary content summarization use case.
signals.review_reason: This blocks the primary user-facing workflow — summarizing content via fabric patterns — when using the Codex provider. User receives 'empty response' with no output, making the tool entirely unusable for this provider. While count=1, it is a complete functional failure of a supported provider. Labeled as bug by maintainers.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: codex empty response
source_issues.evidence: User runs 'echo something | fabric -p summarize' with Codex configured, LLM->FABRIC response content='' and tool outputs 'empty response'. Core use case (summarizing content) is completely broken for Codex users. Issue is closed but no resolution detail visible — user impact is confirmed.

signals.topic: zsh shell tab completion for --listpatterns and --liststrategies does not trigger, reducing CLI discoverability
signals.summary: Fabric's zsh completion script does not activate for --listpatterns and --liststrategies flags, leaving Tab completion inert for users who rely on shell completion for command discovery.
signals.review_reason: zsh shell completion is broken for key CLI commands, impairing discoverability. While it does not block the tool from functioning, it degrades the CLI experience for zsh users and received 7 comments indicating broad impact. Not P0 because it is a UX issue, not a main-flow failure.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: zsh completion does not show item descriptions
source_issues.evidence: fabric --listpatterns <Tab> and fabric --liststrategies <Tab> do nothing in zsh shell. The completion definition exists in completions/_fabric but is not wired correctly. 7 comments on the issue indicate multiple users are affected. Labeled as bug by maintainers.

signals.topic: ENAMETOOLONG unhandled promise rejection crashes CLI — code paste / compiler error / long path
signals.summary: CLI crashes with CRITICAL: Unhandled Promise Rejection! Error: ENAMETOOLONG when users paste multi-line code, encounter compiler error output, or use long file paths. The robustRealpath / lstat path doesn't validate input length and propagates an uncaught exception that kills the entire session.
signals.review_reason: 3 confirmed crash instances with reproducible steps and stack traces. The same uncaught ENAMETOOLONG exception in robustRealpath/lstat flow occurs across distinct triggers (pasting code, reading compiler output, long service account paths). Each crash is session-killing with no graceful fallback — users lose active work mid-session. This is a high-frequency (3/20 issues) session-killing crash that blocks the primary workflow.

source_issues.title: Unhandled Promise Rejection (ENAMETOOLONG) in robustRealpath when pasting code snippets
source_issues.evidence: Pasting multi-line Python code → CLI prepends home dir to code string → lstat gets ENAMETOOLONG → uncaught → CRITICAL crash. Steps to reproduce provided. Android/Termux confirmed.

source_issues.title: ENAMETOOLONG: name too long crash when Next.js compiler error is present in environment
source_issues.evidence: Next.js compiler error (multi-line) gets passed to lstat as file path → ENAMETOOLONG → CLI session killed. Full stack trace provided.

source_issues.title: ENAMETOOLONG - path name to a service account
source_issues.evidence: CLI crashes when attempting to use a path associated with a service account. Unhandled rejection kills session.

signals.topic: Changing Google account handle silently downgrades paying user's subscription tier to free
signals.summary: A paying Ultra subscriber who changed their Google account handle logged out and back into CLI and was treated as free tier. The subscription was correctly shown in the Web App but not in the CLI, causing direct cost loss and access to premium features being unexpectedly revoked.
aliases: subscription tier lost after account handle change
Ultra sub not recognized after account change
CLI treats paying user as free tier
signals.review_reason: Direct cost impact for a paying customer: subscription tier is silently revoked without notice. The user paid for Ultra but is blocked from accessing it in the CLI despite the subscription being active and verifiable. While only 1 issue, the financial impact and complete feature access loss for a paying user warrants P0 under the 'cost loss' criterion.

source_issues.title: Changing google account handle causes gemini CLI to not use your subscription
source_issues.evidence: User is an Ultra subscriber. After changing their Google account handle and re-authenticating in CLI, their tier shows as free. Web App correctly shows Ultra. Adding another account to the family group and logging in with it shows Ultra again, confirming the subscription exists but the CLI fails to recognize it after the handle change.

signals.topic: /auth menu has no exit path — users trapped and must kill entire CLI session
signals.summary: The /auth command presents a screen with no graceful exit option. All failure paths return to the same screen, and the only way to escape is pressing ctrl+c twice to kill the entire CLI session. Users who cannot authenticate are permanently blocked from using the CLI.
signals.review_reason: User is completely blocked from using the CLI. The /auth screen has no exit path — this is a main-flow blocker. The issue author notes it has been reported multiple times before. Only escape is killing the entire process, losing session state. This meets the 'main flow blocked' P0 criterion despite count=1, as it represents a known-regressing complete-use-case blockage.

source_issues.title: Unable to exit /auth for Gemini CLI
source_issues.evidence: Explicitly documented: 'Many issues in the past have reported this one but it's still unresolved.' User is stuck on /auth screen, all failure options lead back to the same screen, and only ctrl+c twice kills the entire CLI. Users unable to authenticate are completely blocked from using the CLI.

signals.topic: Gemini AI silently removes user data (xs:documentation tags) from XML/XSD files during edits
signals.summary: Users who explicitly instructed Gemini to preserve all original data via project mandates find that Gemini silently deletes xs:documentation tags and other documentation from XSD files even during simple info update requests. The user had explicitly required zero data loss and verification before completing tasks.
aliases: original data not preserved despite instructions
signals.review_reason: Silent, irreversible data loss in the primary workflow (file editing). The user had configured explicit data preservation guardrails that were ignored. This is a trust-destroying defect: users cannot safely let the AI modify files with documentation or metadata, requiring manual verification of all changes. Meets 'experience significant decline' and 'data integrity' criteria.

source_issues.title: DATA LOST again and again
source_issues.evidence: User had Gemini.md instructions explicitly prohibiting data deletion (ProjectMandates: Zero Data Loss, Documentation Fidelity). Despite this, Gemini removed xs:documentation tags from their XSD file during a simple information update request. The data loss was discovered after the fact — the AI did not surface any warning or ask for confirmation.

signals.topic: OAuth sign-in permanently blocked for legitimate Gemini Pro paying subscriber
signals.summary: A paying Gemini Pro subscriber (via Google One AI Premium) receives 'This service has been disabled in this account for violation of Terms of Service' when attempting OAuth sign-in to the official Gemini CLI. The account works fine on Gemini Web and API via AI Studio/Vertex, but the CLI OAuth is completely inaccessible — with no third-party tool usage on the account.
aliases: CLI OAuth service disabled for subscriber
signals.review_reason: A paying subscriber is completely locked out of the CLI via OAuth. This is a primary-flow blocker — the user cannot use the product at all despite holding a valid paid subscription. The false-positive ToS violation flag is applied only to the CLI OAuth endpoint, not to other Google AI services, indicating a discriminatory auth block. Counts as 'key feature unavailable' for a paying customer.

source_issues.title: [Auth] Gemini CLI OAuth disabled for Gemini Pro subscriber — no third-party tools used
source_issues.evidence: Paying Pro subscriber (via Google One AI Premium, 5TB) gets 'This service has been disabled in this account for violation of Terms of Service' on official CLI OAuth. Consumer Gemini web and API via AI Studio/Vertex all work normally. User explicitly verified no third-party OAuth connections exist on their account. Entire CLI blocked at authentication.

signals.topic: Tool save/export misses Python dependencies for imports with inline comments, causing exported tools to have incomplete requirements.txt
signals.summary: When saving function-based tools decorated with @tool, imports with inline comments (e.g. `import IPython  # noqa: F401`) are not detected by the regex-based `get_imports()` parser. This results in exported tools (via `make_gradio_app=True`) having incomplete requirements.txt, missing required runtime dependencies.
aliases: Tool save misses commented import dependencies
get_imports regex parser fails on commented imports
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug with a reproducible example. When users export a function-based tool that contains imports with inline comments (a very common pattern in Python codebases), the resulting requirements.txt is missing the imported package. This directly causes exported tools to fail at runtime when deployed, because the required dependency is not installed. The user impact is concrete: broken tool export, missing runtime dependencies, deployment failures.

source_issues.title: Tool save can miss requirements for commented imports
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with reproduction: `@tool` function with `import IPython  # noqa: F401` produces requirements.txt containing only `smolagents`, missing `IPython`. Affects the `make_gradio_app=True` export path.

signals.topic: LocalPythonExecutor timeout does not return control at the configured timeout boundary, causing caller to block until worker completes
signals.summary: The timeout mechanism in LocalPythonExecutor does not respect the configured timeout boundary. When a timeout is hit, the executor's shutdown path waits for the worker thread to finish, so callers do not regain control until the underlying work completes — not at the timeout boundary. PR #1910 introduced a 'robust timeout mechanism' but the current behavior contradicts that promise.
aliases: LocalPythonExecutor timeout blocks caller until worker finishes
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed correctness bug with a minimal reproducible example. The documented timeout feature is broken: instead of returning control to the caller at the configured timeout boundary (e.g., 1 second), the executor blocks until the entire worker task completes (e.g., 3 seconds). This directly blocks the user's main execution flow. PR #1910 explicitly introduced a 'robust timeout mechanism' which the current behavior contradicts. The bug is reproducible on the current main branch.

source_issues.title: BUG: LocalPythonExecutor timeout waits for worker completion before returning
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug with reproduction: `evaluate_python_code(code, timeout_seconds=1)` with a 3-second sleep raises ExecutionTimeoutError after 3.00s elapsed instead of ~1.00s. Root cause is `future.result(timeout=...)` inside `with ThreadPoolExecutor` where the `with` block waits for worker on exit.

signals.topic: Missing LICENSE file blocks institutional adoption and downstream reuse
signals.summary: The repository lacks a top-level LICENSE file, causing automated institutional license checkers to reject the repo and preventing downstream users from legally adapting, redistributing, or citing the code in projects requiring SPDX metadata.
aliases: No LICENSE file for automated license checkers
Institutional license checker rejection due to missing LICENSE file
signals.review_reason: Two separate issues (#523, #395) independently report the same root cause: missing LICENSE file blocks downstream legal reuse and institutional automated tool adoption. Count=2, clearly above noise threshold. The absence of a LICENSE file directly prevents legal use of the codebase in academic/corporate settings that require SPDX-identified licenses.

source_issues.title: Question: would you consider adding a LICENSE file?
source_issues.evidence: Without an explicit license, default copyright is 'all rights reserved', meaning users cannot adapt code, redistribute program.md as a template, or cleanly cite the repo in projects that require SPDX metadata.

source_issues.title: License: add separate MIT license page
source_issues.evidence: Many institutions use an automated license checker that looks for a file called 'LICENSE.txt' or 'LICENSE.md' in the top-level of repo. Without it, automated tools reject the repo, blocking institutional adoption.

signals.topic: Codex provider fails to respect 'never stop' instruction, breaking interactive session workflow
signals.summary: When using the Codex provider, the model ignores the instruction to never stop mid-generation, unlike the Claude provider which respects this directive. This breaks the core interactive session workflow where users expect continuous agent output with ability to pitch in arbitrarily.
aliases: Codex provider not respecting 'never stop' directive
signals.review_reason: The owner (karpathy) explicitly filed this as a provider-level failure: Codex does not respect 'never stop' instruction, breaking the core interactive session loop that is the primary user-facing feature of autoresearch. While count=1, the fact that the repo owner self-reported it with 36 comments demonstrates high user impact — the main workflow is partially broken for Codex users. Not P0 because it only affects one provider (Claude works correctly) and is non-blocking for users willing to switch providers.

source_issues.title: Codex doesn't seem to work?
source_issues.evidence: Codex ignores instruction to never stop, unlike Claude. This breaks the interactive session workflow — the key feature of autoresearch — where users expect to see agent work continuously and pitch in arbitrarily. karpathy (the repo owner) opened this issue, confirming it as a known problem with 36 comments indicating sustained community interest.

signals.topic: SubAgentMiddleware TypeError on startup when model uses RunnableWithFallbacks
signals.summary: resolve_model() raises TypeError: unhashable type: 'RunnableWithFallbacks' when a subagent model is wrapped with BaseChatModel.with_fallbacks(), a standard LangChain pattern for provider redundancy. Breaks SubAgentMiddleware initialization entirely.
signals.review_reason: 3 independent reports of the same TypeError blocking SubAgentMiddleware initialization. Using with_fallbacks() for provider redundancy is standard LangChain practice; this is a regression from v0.3.8. Any user with model fallbacks cannot use subagents at all.

source_issues.title: SubAgents doesn't work with `RunnableFallback` anymore
source_issues.evidence: TypeError on startup. Reproducible with latest version. with_fallbacks() is standard LangChain pattern.

source_issues.title: SubAgentMiddleware.resolve_model fails with RunnableWithFallbacks (TypeError: unhashable type)
source_issues.evidence: Regression from v0.3.8; v0.5 migration broke with_fallbacks support.

source_issues.title: SubAgentMiddleware.resolve_model fails with RunnableWithFallbacks (TypeError: unhashable type)
source_issues.evidence: 3rd report. Root cause identified in resolve_model() and _HARNESS_PROFILES.get().

signals.topic: grep_raw uncapped results cause OOM crash on large codebases
signals.summary: grep_raw has no result cap; running on large repositories buffers gigabytes of results to stdout causing process OOM crash. User reports 7GB of ripgrep output crashing their Linux kernel work.
signals.review_reason: OOM crash confirmed in production on large codebase; causes main workflow to abort. Process crash from unbounded memory allocation is a high-severity runtime blocker.

source_issues.title: Add `max_count` to `grep_raw`
source_issues.evidence: User reports process OOM crash with 7GB ripgrep output buffering. grep_raw has no limit and is used for real work (linux kernel).

signals.topic: Interrupted subagent run corrupts parent thread state, breaking history restoration
signals.summary: When a run is interrupted while a subagent is executing via the task tool, the thread's values.messages contains the subgraph's internal messages instead of the parent graph's messages. This makes it impossible to restore conversation from history — user original message is lost and subagent tool calls are missing.
aliases: subgraph messages leak into parent thread on interruption
signals.review_reason: Data corruption bug — parent thread messages are silently replaced by subgraph internal messages when interruption occurs mid-subagent. Breaks any application relying on thread history for conversation restoration. Confirmed reproducible with checkpointer.

source_issues.title: Interrupted subagent run overwrites parent thread state — history restoration broken
source_issues.evidence: Clear bug with full reproduction steps. Affects all subagent types. References related issues #2629 and #2512 on subgraph state. Any app restoring conversations from thread history is broken for interrupted subagent runs.

signals.topic: CompositeBackend.glob() silently returns zero results when path matches a route
signals.summary: glob() does not strip the route prefix from the search pattern when the path matches a route, causing _glob_search_files to compare the un-stripped pattern against route-relative keys. The result is zero matches with no error or warning. Agents instructed to explore paths like /semantic/tables/ get empty results silently.
aliases: glob silently returns empty on routed paths
signals.review_reason: Silent failure where glob returns zero results with no error when using routed paths. Agents cannot discover files through routed backends, and users get no indication something went wrong. PR with fix is already ready.

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend.glob() does not strip route prefix from pattern when route matches via path
source_issues.evidence: Bug with full reproduction code. Pattern not stripped when route matches. Silent failure — no error returned. PR #2731 is ready with fix.

signals.topic: /offload command crashes with non-OpenAI providers (Anthropic, etc.)
signals.summary: perform_offload() receives messages as raw dicts from aget_state() depending on the checkpointer backend, and passes them to SummarizationMiddleware which calls get_buffer_string(). This raises ValueError: Got unsupported message type for any non-OpenAI provider, making /offload unusable in CLI for Anthropic and other providers.
signals.review_reason: CLI /offload command crashes for any non-OpenAI provider. Offload is a core CLI feature for context management; its complete failure for Anthropic users is a significant UX and workflow blocker. Root cause identified and fix is straightforward.

source_issues.title: `/offload` fails with non-OpenAI providers
source_issues.evidence: Bug with exact error message: ValueError: Got unsupported message type for non-BaseMessage dict. Root cause identified (missing convert_to_messages()). Fix branch ready. History-display path already has the same normalization.

signals.topic: Path traversal vulnerability in FileChatMessageHistory via unsanitized session_id
signals.summary: FileChatMessageHistory constructs file paths using unsanitized user-controlled session_id via RunnableWithMessageHistory's configurable dict. Attackers can read or overwrite arbitrary files on the server using relative traversal (../../etc/passwd) or absolute path injection (/etc/passwd). Both the production implementation and the docstring example are affected.
aliases: unsanitized file path in chat history
signals.review_reason: Server-side arbitrary file read/write vulnerability with clear attack vector: user-controlled session_id in RunnableWithMessageHistory flows directly into os.path.join without sanitization. Both the production implementation (#36890) and the widely-copied docstring example (#36887) are vulnerable. In typical web deployments, session_id originates from request parameters, making this remotely exploitable. High-severity security flaw affecting a core storage component.

source_issues.title: Security: path traversal in FileChatMessageHistory via unsanitized session_id
source_issues.evidence: os.path.join(self.storage_path, self.session_id) allows absolute path injection and relative traversal. Can read arbitrary files as process user. Reported with full reproduction code.

source_issues.title: Security: path traversal in FileChatMessageHistory docstring example via unsanitized session_id
source_issues.evidence: Docstring example in BaseChatMessageHistory shows the vulnerable pattern. Developers copying the example into real applications inherit the path traversal vulnerability.

signals.topic: Importing langchain.agents breaks BaseLLM class construction on Pydantic main
signals.summary: Importing langchain.agents then constructing BaseLLM (or any Pydantic model with dict[...] annotation) causes TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable when using Pydantic main/2.14+, due to __annotations__ mutation in _create_subset_model_v2 breaking Python >=3.10 invariant. Breaks all agent workflows that import langchain.agents before using models.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is broken: importing langchain.agents blocks all subsequent BaseLLM/model instantiation on upcoming Pydantic 2.14+. This is a high-impact compatibility regression that will affect any agent workflow once Pydantic 2.14 releases. Root cause is well-diagnosed (__annotations__ mutation breaking Python invariant), and the impact is confirmed by production CI (logfire). Not P0 only because count=1 and the regression is not yet in a released version of Pydantic.

source_issues.title: Importing langchain.agents breaks BaseLLM class construction on Pydantic main
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: 'function' object is not subscriptable on BaseLLM construction after importing langchain.agents. Affects all code using langchain.agents + any Pydantic model with dict[...] annotation once pydantic 2.14 ships. Impact confirmed by logfire's weekly CI against pydantic main.

signals.topic: Ollama Internal Server Error crashes agent execution workflow
signals.summary: Agent workflows using langchain-ollama fail with ResponseError: Internal Server Error, crashing the entire agent run. The error propagates through langgraph/langgchain stack and results in unhandled exception with TypeError in logging shutdown handler.
signals.review_reason: Agent workflow crashes entirely with unhandled ResponseError from Ollama. While the root cause (Ollama server-side error) is partially external, the crash is non-recoverable and propagates through the entire LangGraph/LangChain stack. The additional TypeError in logging cleanup indicates the error is not gracefully handled. This blocks agent execution for Ollama users.

source_issues.title: ollama._types.ResponseError: Internal Server Error
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows langchain-ollama's _achat_stream_with_aggregation raising ResponseError: Internal Server Error, crashing a RAG agent workflow after fuzzing. Additional TypeError in logging cleanup. Workflow is completely blocked.

signals.topic: OpenAI reasoning content not extracted from API responses in langchain-openai
signals.summary: langchain-openai ignores the 'reasoning' field returned by OpenAI's reasoning-capable models (o1-mini, etc.) during message conversion. Reasoning content is silently dropped instead of being stored in additional_kwargs, preventing users from displaying or processing the model's reasoning process.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (reasoning model output) is silently dropped. Users of reasoning-capable models (o1-mini, o3, etc.) cannot display or process the model's reasoning steps even though the API returns them. This significantly degrades the debugging experience and prevents displaying reasoning in chat UIs. Downgraded to P2 because only 1 issue reported and it's a missing feature rather than a blocking runtime failure.

source_issues.title: feat(openai): Support reasoning content extraction from OpenAI provider responses
source_issues.evidence: response.additional_kwargs does NOT contain the model's reasoning process when using o1-mini. Users who want to display reasoning steps (as shown in native OpenAI interface) cannot access this data through langchain-openai. File-level: libs/partners/openai/langchain_openai/chat_models/base.py _convert_dict_to_message_dict and _convert_delta_to_message_chunk ignore the reasoning field.

signals.topic: Azure OpenAI Responses API reasoning summary not properly extracted
signals.summary: When using Azure-hosted OpenAI models with the Responses API (output_version=responses/v1), some providers return reasoning as 'reasoning_text' items in the content field while leaving summary as empty list. langchain-openai surfaces this provider-specific shape unchanged, causing consumers expecting human-readable reasoning in 'summary' to see empty arrays even when non-trivial reasoning output exists.
aliases: Responses API reasoning content not promoted to summary
signals.review_reason: Reasoning summary is broken for Azure OpenAI Responses API users. Downstream tools (LangGraph checkpoint views, history displays) that rely on the reasoning summary field see empty data even when reasoning was generated. Affects Azure users of reasoning models specifically. P2 due to single-issue count and provider-specific scope.

source_issues.title: AzureChatOpenAI Reasoning Summary not extracted properly
source_issues.evidence: Azure returns reasoning as reasoning_text items in content field with empty summary list. langchain-openai surfaces this unchanged, so consumers using summary (e.g., LangGraph checkpoint/history views) see empty arrays despite non-trivial reasoning output. Reproducer provided shows the exact API response shape.

signals.topic: OpenTelemetry instrumentation causes TypeError crash on agent invocation (1.1.7 regression)
signals.summary: PR #7429 introduced strict GraphCallbackHandler type checking that breaks opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain's monkey-patch, causing LangGraph agents to crash with TypeError at invocation time. Affects AWS Bedrock AgentCore and any production deployment using OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression in 1.1.7 that causes complete crash (TypeError) at agent invocation time for all users with OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation enabled — a common production setup. Explicit TypeError stack trace, reproducible steps, and confirmed production impact on AWS Bedrock. Though single-issue count, the regression severity and production deployment impact warrant P1.

source_issues.title: langgraph 1.1.7 regression: TypeError with opentelemetry-instrumentation-langchain
source_issues.evidence: Regression in 1.1.7: agents crash with TypeError at invocation time when OpenTelemetry instrumentation is active. Full stack trace provided. Affects AWS Bedrock AgentCore with aws-opentelemetry-distro. Reproducible with LangchainInstrumentor().instrument() + create_react_agent().ainvoke(). Crash occurs at _init_base_manager during BaseCallbackManager.__init__() call intercepted by monkey-patch.

signals.topic: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud causing 2-3x cost waste
signals.summary: Tool calls exceeding ~3 minutes on LangGraph Cloud are silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both complete successfully, resulting in duplicate work and cost waste.
signals.review_reason: Silent duplicate execution of tool calls causing 2-3x redundant cost — a direct cost loss in production. The duplication is silent (no error shown to user), making it particularly dangerous. Affects the critical path of long-running sub-agent workflows, which are a primary use case for LangGraph Cloud.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Tool calls taking >3 minutes on LangGraph Cloud are silently re-dispatched from checkpoint while original still runs. Both complete with identical arguments. Confirmed 2-3x redundant work and cost. Affects SubAgentMiddleware with sub-agents taking 3-10 minutes. Duplicate runs appear in trace with identical tool call arguments.

signals.topic: Agent infinite looping until recursion limit reached (1.0.6 regression from 0.6.x)
signals.summary: Text-to-SQL LangGraph agents loop indefinitely until hitting recursion limit in version 1.0.6, despite correct stop conditions in the prompt. Regression from 0.6.x versions.
signals.review_reason: Complete workflow failure: agent loops indefinitely wasting LLM calls and compute until recursion limit is hit, producing no output. Explicitly a regression from 0.6x to 1.0.6 — user had to downgrade to unblock work. Main flow is fully blocked.

source_issues.title: LangGraph [1.0.6] Bug - Agent infinite looping until recursion limit error is hit
source_issues.evidence: Agent created with 1.0.6 loops indefinitely despite proper stop conditions in the prompt. Same configuration works on 0.6x. Root cause: agent keeps re-executing tool calls that return errors and never terminates. Complete workflow failure — agent does not produce any output.

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared metadata causing thread_id leakage between invocations
signals.summary: ensure_config assigns the metadata key by reference without calling .copy(), so configurable values like thread_id get injected into the shared base config metadata. After first invocation, subsequent calls see leaked data from previous invocations.
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption: ensure_config mutates shared base config metadata by reference, causing thread_id values from prior invocations to leak into subsequent calls. This leads to hard-to-debug cross-session contamination and non-deterministic behavior. Well-confirmed with 8 discussion comments and clear reproduction path.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: ensure_config passes metadata dict by reference (no .copy()). After first graph.invoke(), the shared base config's metadata is contaminated with previous invocation data (e.g., thread_id from prior call). Subsequent invocations see {'ls_integration': 'langchain_create_agent', 'thread_id': '<previous_thread_id>'} — non-deterministic behavior based on invocation history. 8 comments confirming the bug with code examples.

signals.topic: RetryPolicy jitter applied after max_interval cap, violating documented timing contract
signals.summary: When RetryPolicy(jitter=True, max_interval=X) is used, the actual sleep can exceed max_interval by up to 1 second because jitter is added AFTER the min() cap. The documented contract (max_interval = 'maximum amount of time that may elapse between retries') is silently violated.
signals.review_reason: Violates the documented RetryPolicy contract — max_interval is described as a hard cap on sleep time but jitter breaks it. Silent timing deviation that can cause issues with rate limiting expectations and retry throttling. However, impact is subtle (not a crash/block), making it P2 priority.

source_issues.title: RetryPolicy: jitter can cause sleep to exceed max_interval
source_issues.evidence: Jitter (random uniform 0-1) is added AFTER min(max_interval, ...) cap, so actual sleep = min(max_interval, ...) + jitter, can be up to max_interval + 1s. Documented contract says max_interval is 'maximum amount of time that may elapse between retries'. Clear code location identified in source.

signals.topic: v2 ADD-only pipeline missing semantic conflict resolution — duplicate and contradictory memories stored permanently
signals.summary: The v2.0.0 ADD-only extraction architecture does not resolve contradictory facts. Adding 'my name is Alice' then 'my name is Bob' stores both as separate ADD events permanently. Both appear in get_all() and search results, degrading retrieval quality. MD5 hash dedup only catches exact duplicates, not semantically similar or contradictory content.

source_issues.title: ADD-only architecture doesn't implement conflict resolution for semantically similar memories
source_issues.evidence: Both contradictory facts stored as separate ADD events. Documentation promises 'Latest truth wins when contradictions detected' but only MD5 hash dedup is implemented. get_all() returns 2 results instead of 1.

source_issues.title: fix: semantic conflict resolution missing in v2 ADD-only pipeline

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor has no runtime sandboxing — LLM-generated code executes with full host privileges
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess without any runtime security controls. The only safeguard is a UserWarning at initialization which is easily suppressed in production (e.g., -W ignore). This creates a direct attack surface for indirect prompt injection: untrusted data can cause the LLM to generate malicious code that steals credentials (SSH keys, cloud tokens, env vars), destroys data, or pivots to internal networks — all with the privileges of the Python process.
aliases: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
signals.review_reason: 运行时无沙箱保护，UserWarning 可被生产配置轻易抑制，用户在真实部署中面临凭证窃取、数据销毁等严重后果。虽然是 single issue，但威胁路径明确（prompt injection → 代码执行 → 凭据外泄），影响的是关键功能（代码执行器）的安全性，默认 keep=false 会漏掉高危真实威胁。标记 P1 因 count=1 不满足 P0 硬约束条件。

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: Affected code writes LLM-generated code to disk then executes via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with no sandboxing, filesystem isolation, or network restrictions. UserWarning at init is trivially suppressed in production. Attack scenario demonstrated: prompt injection leading to credential theft via subprocess call to exfiltrate ~/.ssh/id_rsa. Severity rated HIGH per OWASP ASI-09. Evidence from agent-audit security scanner.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock image-to-text (captioning) completely broken — ImageContent metadata not forwarded to Bedrock models
signals.summary: The BedrockChatCompletionService fails to interpret image binaries when passed as ImageContent, returning responses like 'I don't see an image provided'. Works with Azure OpenAI but silently fails on Bedrock, making image captioning unusable on that backend.
signals.review_reason: Image captioning is a key feature that is completely non-functional on Bedrock. The bug is reproducible with clear evidence (model returns explicit 'I don't see an image' message). Confirmed to work via raw Python API, isolating the issue to SK's Bedrock connector metadata handling. Affects users who rely on Bedrock for multimodal tasks.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Amazon BedrockChatCompletionService image-to-text (captioning) not working
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with reproduction code: ImageContent with image/png/jpeg/bmp MIME types all return 'I don't see an image provided' response. Python raw API calls work correctly. Key feature (image captioning) completely non-functional on Bedrock.

signals.topic: Python Redis connector corrupts search indexes — PREFIX split character-by-character in FT.CREATE
signals.summary: The Python Redis connector passes a plain string to redis-py's IndexDefinition(prefix=...), causing it to be iterated character-by-character. This silently creates unintended single-character prefixes, corrupting index matching in multi-collection shared Redis deployments.
signals.review_reason: Data correctness issue: indexes silently match unintended keys across collections in shared Redis environments, leading to cross-collection data corruption. Bug is latent and silent (tests pass) but causes incorrect search results. Root cause and wire-level evidence confirmed. Affects production multi-collection deployments.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Redis connector sends malformed `FT.CREATE PREFIX` (one prefix per character of collection name)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in python/semantic_kernel/connectors/redis.py:281. Wire capture shows 'PREFIX 27 r e d i s...' instead of 'PREFIX 1 redis_json_list_data_model:'. In multi-collection shared Redis, collections with overlapping characters register overlapping prefixes and match each other's keys — data corruption. Bug is silent on Redis Stack (tests pass).

signals.topic: OpenAPI/Manifest plugin does not respect custom HttpResponseContentReader or RestApiOperationResponseFactory
signals.summary: When importing a plugin from an API Manifest, custom delegates set via HttpResponseContentReader or RestApiOperationResponseFactory in ApiManifestPluginParameters.FunctionExecutionParameters are silently ignored. Users expecting the same behavior as direct OpenAPI plugins get unexpected results with no error.
aliases: Manifest plugin custom response factory not used
signals.review_reason: Custom response handling is a documented extensibility mechanism that is silently ignored when using API Manifest-based plugins versus direct OpenAPI. The behavior inconsistency (OpenAPI works, Manifest doesn't) is a clear functional gap with no error message. Forces users to abandon their custom response logic.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: creating plugin from OpenAPI/Manifest does not respect custom `HttpResponseContentReader` or `RestApiOperationResponseFactory`
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer repo demonstrates WeatherGovAsOpenApi passes (callbacks invoked) while WeatherGovAsApiManifest fails (callbacks ignored). Custom response handling is a core extensibility feature; silently ignoring it breaks user expectations and forces workarounds.

signals.topic: Chat Completion Agent calls functions outside the allowed FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto list (function spillover)
signals.summary: When explicitly providing a restricted function list in FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto([...]), the ChatCompletionAgent still calls functions not in that list. The save_stop_condition function, explicitly excluded, is called anyway. This breaks user intent and causes unintended side effects.
signals.review_reason: Agent autonomy is a primary value proposition. When users explicitly restrict the function set, the agent still calls excluded functions — violating user intent and potentially causing data corruption (e.g., save_stop_condition modifying state unexpectedly). Multiple workaround attempts documented as failing, confirming this is a real blocking issue.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Functions spillover in Chat Completion Agent
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer code shows save_stop_condition called despite being excluded from FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto list. Documentation states only provided functions will be advertised. User tried UseImmutableKernel=true, moving instructions to template — all workarounds failed. Core agent autonomy feature is broken.

signals.topic: Memory feature stops working after reaching context/token limits — refuses to create new memories, ignores existing ones
signals.summary: The memorize/memory feature becomes inconsistent or stops working entirely after the context window reaches certain limits. Users report being unable to create new memories, the feature getting stuck after ~300 lines, and Codex sometimes refusing to add content to memory even when explicitly asked. Memory files also appear to not be read on session start, requiring manual re-read. This appears correlated with account switching and reaching token window thresholds.
aliases: memory files not read on startup
signals.review_reason: P1: Two separate issues with count=2 describing memory feature failures from different angles. Issue #18750 shows memory creation stops after reaching token thresholds (core feature blocked). Issue #18738 shows memory files not read on startup (core feature bypassed). Both represent critical feature breakdown for a key Codex capability. Not P0 because they are not simultaneous — they are separate manifestations that may have different root causes.

source_issues.title: memory creation refusing / not adding new memorise up to a point
source_issues.evidence: Memory creation gets stuck after ~300 lines despite having 300k token context window available. Codex refuses to add content when asked explicitly. User suspects functionality is lost after reaching the 250k-token window 6 times. Behavior is inconsistent — works sometimes but then completely stops.

source_issues.title: Memory apparently ignored by Codex until specifically asked to read it
source_issues.evidence: Memory file (~/.codex/memories/conventional_commits.md) is never read on session start. Codex ignores its own stored instructions (Conventional Commits format, Co-Authored trailer) until user explicitly asks it to re-read the memory. Demonstrates that memory is a core feature being silently bypassed.

signals.topic: Auto-compact/hand-off loses critical task context during execution, causing Codex to deviate from user intent
signals.summary: When the context window becomes highly filled and Codex triggers auto-compact mid-execution, the handoff summary becomes incomplete or distorted. The model then continues from a degraded internal state and solves a different problem than requested, even on small fixes. Users observe the model initially understanding the task correctly, then after auto-compact, working on a different goal entirely. This looks like instruction-following failure but is actually a compact/handoff bug that silently corrupts task state.
signals.review_reason: P0: Auto-compact is a main flow feature that silently corrupts task state mid-execution. The model appears to follow instructions correctly initially, then delivers a completely different solution after compact — without any user-visible error. This blocks reliable automated coding work, especially for longer sessions where the context window fills up. Clear user impact evidence: user provided concrete example of model changing animation approach post-compact vs. original request. Count=1 but review_reason provides strong user impact evidence (silent task corruption, reproducibility on small fixes, blocks automated coding workflow).

source_issues.title: Codex auto-compact loses critical task details and causes wrong execution, even on small fixes
source_issues.evidence: Auto-compact during execution causes the model to lose the original task intent and constraints. After compact, model changed the requested animation approach entirely (removed masked conic ring instead of fixing the artifact). User explicitly states this is a product-level compact/handoff issue, not a model capability issue. Reproducible even on very small 17-line fixes. The failure is silent — no error is shown, so users may not realize the task was corrupted.

signals.topic: CLI sessions become permanently unrecoverable after WebSocket disconnects on Windows (~37-40 minutes)
signals.summary: On Windows 11, Codex CLI sessions work normally for ~37-40 minutes, then begin failing with WebSocket disconnect/reconnect behavior. Once a session enters this failed state, it can never recover — opening the same session and sending a prompt triggers long reconnect loops with no resolution. Only workaround is starting a brand-new session. This cycle repeats: new sessions eventually fail the same way after 37-40 minutes. Server-side session timeout of ~40 minutes is the suspected root cause, making the session unrecoverable at the transport layer.
signals.review_reason: P1: High-impact Windows-specific session reliability issue. WebSocket disconnects make sessions permanently unusable after ~40 minutes, forcing users to abandon work and start over. This is not a one-off network issue — it is reproducible and consistent. User impact: main coding workflow is blocked. Cannot be P0 because count=1, but review_reason provides strong evidence (reproducible timestamps, detailed logs, clear workaround). This is distinct from #18709 which is about session history not appearing in desktop app.

source_issues.title: Codex CLI sessions become unrecoverable after ~37-40 minutes on Windows 11 after websocket disconnects
source_issues.evidence: Session becomes permanently poisoned after WebSocket disconnects. Opening the same session and sending a prompt triggers long reconnect attempts that never succeed. Fresh sessions work again temporarily but fail after ~37-40 minutes. Timestamps confirm reproducible ~37-40 minute failure window. User logs show retry attempts up to 5 times with falling back to HTTP. Main workflow is blocked — user must abandon sessions and start over repeatedly.

signals.topic: False positive rate limit errors blocking Codex usage despite not having reached limits
signals.summary: Codex incorrectly reports 'You've hit your usage limit' errors, preventing users from resuming or continuing sessions even when they have not actually reached their quota. This blocks the main coding workflow — users cannot work when falsely told they've exceeded their limits. The issue occurs on Codex Plus subscriptions.
signals.review_reason: P1: Billing/usage reporting error that directly blocks user from performing work. When a paid user is told they have hit limits when they have not, the main product workflow is completely stopped. Count=1 but strong user impact (paid subscription blocked from working). Combined with #18742 (/status showing stale limits) and #18709 (IDE extension cannot load chats), this forms a pattern of state/session management failures.

source_issues.title: Cannot use Codex due hitting the limits, though I didn't reach them

User explicitly states they did NOT reach the limits. This is a blocking error that prevents the main coding workflow entirely. User provided uploaded thread as evidence.

signals.topic: IDE extension requires full desktop app to be open to load chat history — dependency breaks developer workflow
signals.summary: On Windows, the VS Code Codex extension cannot load chat history unless the full Codex desktop application is already open. This is a new regression — this dependency did not exist before. For Business subscription users who rely on the IDE extension for their primary coding workflow, this adds unnecessary friction and breaks the expected standalone IDE experience. Users must launch two separate apps to use one.
aliases: IDE extension needs desktop app open
signals.review_reason: P1: Regression that breaks the expected standalone IDE extension workflow. Business users are impacted. Explicitly stated as a regression (worked before). Count=1 but clear user impact (two-app requirement for one workflow). This is a UX regression for professional users, not a trivial inconvenience.

source_issues.title: We have to open Codex App to load chats in IDE extension
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states this is a regression — the behavior worked before without needing the desktop app. Business subscription users are affected, meaning this impacts professional users. Opening VS Code requires also opening desktop app to see chats, breaking the standalone IDE extension workflow.

signals.topic: Sandbox agent fails to start on Windows due to Unix-specific path resolution
signals.summary: Windows users cannot use sandbox agents at all. Two related failures: (1) Import of agents.sandbox.sandboxes fails with ModuleNotFoundError: fcntl because Unix-only backend is eagerly imported; (2) WorkspaceStartError when using local sandbox mode on Windows due to hardcoded Unix path resolution. Both are platform-level blocks for Windows users.
signals.review_reason: Two related but distinct Windows platform blocks: (1) entire sandbox import crashes due to Unix-only fcntl module; (2) even if import were fixed, WorkspaceStartError prevents local sandbox usage. Together these make the sandbox feature completely unusable on Windows — a major platform-level user impact.

source_issues.title: WorkspaceStartError on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Windows users get WorkspaceStartError when trying to use local sandbox mode. Error shows resolve-workspace-path-f8e24896b498 not found in PATH — Unix-only binary referenced on Windows.

source_issues.title: Windows: import agents.sandbox.sandboxes fails with ModuleNotFoundError: fcntl
source_issues.evidence: Import of agents.sandbox.sandboxes immediately crashes on Windows with ModuleNotFoundError: fcntl. Unix-only backend is eagerly imported at package load time, blocking all sandbox functionality on Windows.

signals.topic: RealtimeAgent tool execution causes agent to get stuck with active-response conflict error
signals.summary: When a tool is registered to a RealtimeAgent and the tool executes while a response is in progress, a RealtimeError ('Conversation already has an active response in progress') is raised, causing the agent to hang indefinitely. The root cause is in _send_tool_output which creates a response.create event without checking for an active response.
aliases: active response conflict in realtime tools
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking: realtime agent gets permanently stuck when a tool executes during an active response, forcing the user to restart the conversation. Clear runtime error with concrete stack trace and explicit user impact description.

source_issues.title: Realtime Tools cause agent response to cut off.
source_issues.evidence: Agent gets stuck and waits for customer request to respond after RealtimeError is raised during async tool execution. Explicitly described as 'This causes the agent to get stuck' — a main flow block.

signals.topic: Background run-loop exceptions are silently swallowed in stream_events() — result appears successful with no error
signals.summary: When Runner.run_streamed() is used with a sandbox agent, any exception raised in the background run loop before the first stream event is silently swallowed. The result returns with final_output=None, new_items=[], raw_responses=0 with no indication of failure. Users must manually inspect result.run_loop_task.exception() to find the real error.
aliases: stream result appears clean but task failed
signals.review_reason: Significant debugging experience degradation: tasks fail silently and return apparently-clean results, hiding fatal errors from users. Forces manual inspection of internal task exception state. Users cannot detect failures through normal observation — they must know to check run_loop_task.exception().

source_issues.title: Surface run-loop exceptions in stream_events() for early failures
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states 'exception raised in the background run loop before the first stream event is silently swallowed' and result 'appears to finish cleanly (final_output=None, new_items=[], raw_responses=0) with no indication that a fatal error occurred'. Forces users to dig into internal task state to find failures.

signals.topic: Hosted tools not supported with ChatCompletions API — SandboxAgent unusable with Azure OpenAI and similar providers
signals.summary: When using SandboxAgent with the ChatCompletions API (e.g., Azure OpenAI), a UserError is raised: 'Hosted tools are not supported with the ChatCompletions API'. This blocks users from using the sandbox feature with non-OpenAI providers that only support Chat Completions mode.

signals.review_reason: Key feature (SandboxAgent) becomes unusable when using ChatCompletions API providers (Azure OpenAI and other OpenAI-compatible backends). The error explicitly says 'Hosted tools are not supported' — a clear feature incompatibility that blocks the primary use case for non-OpenAI users.
