signals.topic: Tool names containing spaces are silently renamed without warning — causes hard-to-debug mismatches
signals.summary: In transform_string_function_style, spaces in tool names are replaced with underscores before the warning comparison check. This means tool names with spaces are silently transformed (e.g., 'My Tool' -> 'my_tool') with no log warning, making tool name mismatches very difficult to debug.
aliases: tool name space replacement warning bypass
signals.review_reason: Silent behavior that produces wrong tool names without any warning or log entry, directly causing mismatches between expected and actual tool names. Hard to debug because no error is raised and nothing is logged. User impact is real but non-blocking.

source_issues.title: transform_string_function_style silently transforms space-containing names without warning
source_issues.evidence: Logic bug causes tool names with spaces to be silently lowercased and space-replaced without triggering the warning. Users defining tools with names containing spaces get silently renamed with no log entry, making tool name mismatches difficult to debug.

signals.topic: Responses API multi-turn conversations fail with 400 errors on turn 2
signals.summary: When passing response.output back as input for multi-turn conversations, the SDK causes 400 errors on turn 2 — either 'Unknown parameter' due to model_dump() fabricating null fields (status: null, encrypted_content: null), or 'Item type message was provided without its required preceding item of type reasoning' due to an undocumented pairing constraint.
aliases: Multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
Responses API: undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint breaks multi-turn conversations
signals.review_reason: Both issues block the core multi-turn conversation workflow. #3008: model_dump() (a Python SDK method) produces invalid API payloads — this is a direct library defect. #3009: undocumented pairing constraint silently breaks the most common pattern for continuing conversations (filtering to messages only). Together they make multi-turn Responses API usage unreliable. Evidence: OpenClaw (64.9k forks) broke in production. Despite count=2 < 3, the review_reason provides explicit production-breakage evidence and a 0.95 confidence, warranting P0 for a core workflow blocker.

source_issues.title: Responses API: multi-turn conversations 400 on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input
source_issues.evidence: model_dump() fabricates status: None, encrypted_content: None for fields the API never returned. API rejects null unknown parameters with 400: Unknown parameter. Also triggers pairing constraint error. Confirmed affecting OpenClaw (64.9k forks) in production.

source_issues.title: Responses API: undocumented reasoning+message pairing constraint breaks multi-turn conversations
source_issues.evidence: API requires reasoning+message items as consecutive pairs in input. Filtering response.output to keep only messages (common pattern) produces orphaned items → 400: Item type message was provided without its required preceding item of type reasoning. Reproduced across all 5 SDKs and curl. Broke OpenClaw (64.9k forks) in production.

signals.topic: Response.output_text and responses.parse fail when output_text content item has text: null
signals.summary: When the Responses API returns an output_text content item with text=null (valid API behavior), the Python SDK's Response.output_text property raises TypeError (attempting to concatenate None), and both strict parsing and structured responses.parse() also fail.
aliases: Response.output_text fails to handle null text values in content items
Output_text property TypeError on null text from API
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bugs (#3063, #3011) with the same root cause: the Python SDK cannot handle valid API responses where output_text.text is null. #3011: accessing the output_text convenience property raises TypeError on null values. #3063: strict parsing and structured responses.parse() also fail. Both are library defects that break parsing of valid API payloads.

source_issues.title: Response.output_text and responses.parse fail when an output_text item has text: null
source_issues.evidence: Two affected layers: (1) strict response parsing rejects ResponseOutputText.text = null with model validation error, (2) parsed responses can still attempt structured parsing on output_text items with text=null causing downstream failures. The API can return valid output_text items with null text. SDK should accept nullable output_text.text values.

source_issues.title: Response.output_text fails to handle null text values in content items
source_issues.evidence: When the Responses API returns output_text items with text:null, accessing Response.output_text raises TypeError because it attempts to join() a list containing None values. The output_text property aggregates all output_text items via text concatenation, and fails silently (or with TypeError) when text is null.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely with file status stuck at in_progress
signals.summary: The upload_and_poll() method can hang forever because the vector store file can remain stuck at status=in_progress indefinitely with no error, and last_error stays null, so the polling never terminates.
aliases: Vector store file upload_and_poll indefinite hang
signals.review_reason: Blocking library-level defect: the upload_and_poll() method (a Python SDK polling convenience method) hangs indefinitely with no timeout and no error signal. The file stays in_progress forever with null last_error, so the polling loop has no termination condition. This is a main-flow failure — users cannot use the vector store file upload API reliably.

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: upload_and_poll() never returns when vector store file stays in_progress indefinitely. last_error is null so no termination signal. The raw file is processed but the vector store indexing hangs forever. No timeout mechanism exists in the library. Confirmed on openai==2.31.0, Python 3.12, April 15-16 2026.

signals.topic: AsyncResponses.parse() memory leak — unbounded pydantic SchemaValidator/Serializer allocation
signals.summary: Every call to AsyncResponses.parse() with structured outputs allocates new SchemaValidator/Serializer objects (heavy Rust objects) that never get freed, causing linear memory growth and eventual OOM in long-running servers.
aliases: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
Unbounded pydantic schema rebuild memory leak in responses.parse
signals.review_reason: Well-documented, severe memory leak in the Python SDK's responses.parse() path. Every structured output parse call allocates unbounded Rust objects (SchemaValidator/Serializer) that are never freed, causing linear RSS growth and eventual OOM in long-running servers. Root cause is precisely identified in the library code (openai/lib/_parsing/_responses.py). Flame graph evidence provided. This is a main-flow failure for any server using structured outputs.

source_issues.title: Async Responses Structured Outputs Memory leak
source_issues.evidence: openai/lib/_parsing/_responses.py calls construct_type_unchecked with ParsedResponse[TextFormatT] where TextFormatT is unresolved. Pydantic model_rebuild always returns False, so _built_memo is never populated, and a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) is allocated on every single responses.parse() call. RSS grows linearly with request count. Flame graph provided. Impact: long-running servers eventually OOM.

signals.topic: PydanticUserError in multiprocess forkserver workers with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12
signals.summary: In forkserver multiprocessing setups, PydanticUserError ('Pydantic models should inherit from BaseModel, BaseModel cannot be instantiated directly') is raised intermittently (0.6-9.5% error rate) when deserializing chat completion responses, causing production failures.
aliases: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True in multiprocess forkserver workers
signals.review_reason: Production-impacting bug: in forkserver multiprocessing (a common production pattern), the Python SDK raises PydanticUserError with 0.6-9.5% error rate when deserializing responses. This is caused by the library's defer_build mechanism conflicting with pydantic 2.12's schema resolution. Exact root cause identified in library code path (openai/_models.py). Impact is significant for any production server using the SDK in a multiprocess forkserver setup.

source_issues.title: PydanticUserError with defer_build=True and pydantic 2.12 in multiprocess forkserver workers
source_issues.evidence: In forkserver multiprocessing with ~700 workers processing millions of requests: with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=true (default) ~0.6% error rate growing over time; with DEFER_PYDANTIC_BUILD=false ~9.5% error rate. Root cause: construct() calls _get_extra_fields_type which triggers model_rebuild with hardcoded _parent_namespace_depth=5. When call stack depth doesn't contain openai types namespace (common in forkserver), model_rebuild fails and raises PydanticUserError. Full stack trace provided.

signals.topic: Security scanner false positives block legitimate skill publication
signals.summary: The OpenClaw security scanner produces widespread false-positive 'suspicious' flags on legitimate, non-malicious skills, requiring developers to file appeals and blocking publication. Multiple independent developers across different skill domains (API clients, financial analysis, behavior-modification, network tools, P2P runtimes) are all flagged, indicating a systemic scanner over-sensitivity problem rather than isolated incidents.
aliases: False positive security flags on legitimate skills
signals.review_reason: 12 independent developers across diverse legitimate skill categories (API clients, financial tools, behavior-modification, P2P networking, agent registries, analysis tools) are all being flagged as 'suspicious' by the same scanner. This is a systemic over-sensitivity problem: the scanner flags keyword patterns (crypto/wallet/OAuth in dependency internals, curl+API-key in legitimate API clients, instructional language in analysis skills) that have nothing to do with actual malicious behavior. The root causes are: (1) keyword-based matching on third-party library internals, (2) inability to distinguish benign instructional patterns from prompt injection, (3) over-broad capability chip heuristics. This directly blocks the main publishing workflow: skills cannot be listed as clean without moderator intervention, forcing developers to file appeals. Issue #1733 shows a developer made 7 attempts and still cannot get their legitimate trading-assistance skill cleared. This is a high-frequency (12 reports in 2 days), high-impact (publish-blocking), user-visible degradation of the core marketplace trust model.

source_issues.title: False-positive signals on jimcollinson/x0x v0.17.4
source_issues.evidence: Scanner flags Node.js binding code that never runs in skill install path; financial/crypto keywords from pip internals also flagged. Multiple capability chips (wallet, OAuth, purchases, signing) applied incorrectly.

signals.topic: Account-level ban blocks legitimate developer from all write operations
signals.summary: A developer with multiple legitimate published skills was fully locked out of their ClawHub account: all write operations (publish, login) return Unauthorized, the web interface is inaccessible, and no email notification was sent. Read operations still work, indicating an account-level ban rather than token revocation.
aliases: Write operations blocked after legitimate publishing
signals.review_reason: This is a single report but represents complete account lockout — the developer can no longer publish skills, respond to issues, or manage existing listings. The key evidence of user impact: (1) 'clawhub publish' returns Unauthorized, (2) 'clawhub login' fails, (3) web interface login blocked, (4) no notification email received. This is a severe auth permission issue that renders the platform unusable for the affected developer. The claim that the ban was a 'false positive' (same automated scanner over-sensitivity from PP-001) makes this a direct consequence of the scanner problem.

source_issues.title: Account @qiji0802 banned as false positive — legitimate skill publishing blocked
source_issues.evidence: Developer claims legitimate productivity skills (GEO Master, Sentiment Compass, InvoiceGuard, etc.) were published via CLI. All write operations now return Unauthorized. Web login blocked. No notification sent. Read ops (search, inspect) still work — suggesting account-level ban, not just token revocation. Developer unable to publish updates or new skills.

signals.topic: Publish form version field rejects valid minor/major semver bumps
signals.summary: The skill version publish form only accepts the auto-populated patch bump; any manually edited semver value (including valid minor and major bumps like 1.6.0, 2.0.0) is rejected with a client-side validation error stating 'Version must be valid semver', even though the entered value is perfectly valid semver.
aliases: Semver validation bug in publish form
Version field rejects valid version numbers
Cannot publish minor/major version bumps via web UI
signals.review_reason: A specific, reproducible bug in the web publishing UI that prevents skill maintainers from cutting minor or major releases through the web form. While a CLI workaround exists, this is a direct workflow block for web UI users. The misleading error message makes it harder to diagnose, and the forced workaround (mislabeling version numbers) creates downstream confusion for skill consumers reading changelogs.

source_issues.title: Publish skill page: version field rejects valid minor/major bumps with 'must be valid semver' error
source_issues.evidence: Exact reproduction steps provided: auto-fill suggests 1.5.2 (accepted); manually changing to 1.6.0 (valid semver) triggers error. The error message is misleading — it says 'must be valid semver (e.g. 1.0.0)' implying format is the problem, but the actual rule appears to only accept the auto-suggested patch bump. Workaround forces developer to mislabel real minor releases as patches, breaking CHANGELOG semantics for consumers.

signals.topic: Cannot unpublish/remove outdated skill versions — no self-service deletion
signals.summary: Skill owners cannot unpublish or delete old skill versions from the marketplace through the web interface. Renaming creates a duplicate entry rather than updating, leaving outdated/beta versions visible and conflicting with new ones.
aliases: Duplicate skill entries from rename workflow
signals.review_reason: Lack of self-service unpublishing forces developers to file support tickets for routine maintenance. The rename workaround creating duplicate entries rather than updating adds further confusion. While not blocking core publishing, this creates marketplace pollution with invalid skill versions visible to consumers.

source_issues.title: Request to remove my outdated skills (conflict due to rename)
source_issues.evidence: Developer has 3 outdated skills (vs-test, valuescan-monitor-skill-beta, valuescan-data-skill) with replacements already published. No UI option to unpublish. Rename attempt created new entries instead of updating, leaving old versions conflicting with new ones. Old skills provide no valid service and confuse users.

signals.topic: Newly published skill not searchable via ClawHub search
signals.summary: A newly uploaded skill with slug name 'cloudq' cannot be found via the ClawHub search interface, preventing the skill from being discovered by potential users after publication.
aliases: Skill not appearing in search results
Search index not updating after publish
signals.review_reason: The skill is technically published but undiscoverable via the primary marketplace discovery mechanism (search). This defeats the purpose of publishing — a skill no one can find is effectively unavailable. The user impact is clear: no search results returned for the exact slug name.

source_issues.title: Can not search skill from Clawhub
source_issues.evidence: Developer published skill with slug 'cloudq' but search returns no results. Screenshots in the issue show the search returning empty. The skill is published and visible at its direct URL but not discoverable through search.

signals.topic: system.run exec approval policy bypass via shell wrappers
signals.summary: Shell wrapper forms (powershell -Command, cmd /c, etc.) are not parsed during policy evaluation, allowing inner destructive commands to bypass exec approval rules while the outer command passes review.
signals.review_reason: Exec approval policy is a core security control; its bypass is a meaningful user impact. A connected agent can execute destructive commands that should have been blocked, bypassing the intended exec approval policy. This is not theoretical — the issue provides concrete payloads and cites that the shell wrapper bypass (item 2 of 2) was left unfixed after the partial fix in PR #186. Confidence is capped at 0.75 because the bypass has count=1 and the fix has been partially addressed (env var vector fixed), leaving only the shell wrapper vector open.

source_issues.title: [Security] system.run: env variable injection and shell wrapper approval bypass
source_issues.evidence: Policy evaluates fullCommand once before execution without parsing payloads inside shell wrappers. Commands like ['powershell', '-Command', 'Remove-Item -Recurse -Force C:\important'] can bypass rules like 'Remove-Item *' if the outer command is allowed. PR #186 (merged) fixed the env-var injection vector but the shell wrapper bypass remains unfixed per Repo Assist issue #127.

signals.topic: One-shot cron deleteAfterRun deletes and rebinds live DM session, causing irrecoverable context loss
signals.summary: When a non-default agent's Signal/Telegram DM has a one-shot cron reminder with deleteAfterRun:true and sessionTarget pointing to the live session, the live session binding is deleted and rebound to a fresh empty session. The user's next message lands in a blank transcript and the agent forgets the entire conversation.
signals.review_reason: One-shot cron jobs with deleteAfterRun can delete the live DM session binding itself and replace it with a fresh empty session. Gateway logs show three sequential session rebindings across concurrent reminder jobs. User's conversation context was completely lost — agent responded with 'I don't have context' on next user message. This is a main-flow failure with irrecoverable state loss.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: one-shot cron deleteAfterRun can delete and rebind a live non-default DM session when sessionTarget resolves to current/session:*
source_issues.evidence: Live DM session key rebound across three reminder jobs: pre-existing populated session (messages=66) deleted, replaced by two fresh sessions (messages=0). Next user reply landed in empty session; agent responded 'I don't have context'. Full gateway log timeline provided.

signals.topic: openclaw security audit command hangs indefinitely with no output
signals.summary: The CLI security audit command hangs forever on every invocation with zero output, making the entire security audit workflow inaccessible.
signals.review_reason: The `openclaw security audit` command is completely non-functional — it hangs indefinitely on all flag variants with zero output before timing out. This blocks an entire security workflow. Gateway is otherwise healthy and other commands work, ruling out systemic issues.

source_issues.title: Bug: `openclaw security audit` hangs indefinitely (no output)
source_issues.evidence: All three flag variants (--deep, --json, no-flag) hang to timeout (15-20s) with exit code 124 and zero output. Gateway is healthy and other commands (status, gateway status, cron list) work fine.

signals.topic: MCP stdio server processes orphaned on session end — progressive RAM leak up to multi-GB
signals.summary: MCP stdio servers spawned per session via npx are never terminated when sessions end. Processes accumulate over time: 41 orphaned context7-mcp processes consuming 2.4GB RAM observed on a 30GB server. Related issues #60656, #69145, #65694 confirm the same pattern.
signals.review_reason: MCP stdio server processes are spawned per session but never cleaned up. 41 orphaned processes consumed 2.4GB RAM on a 30GB server. RAM consumption grows linearly with usage, eventually risking service stability. This is a documented, reproducible resource exhaustion issue with corroborating references #60656, #69145, #65694.

source_issues.title: Bug: MCP stdio server processes orphaned on session end — 2.4GB RAM leak from context7-mcp
source_issues.evidence: 41 orphaned context7-mcp processes consuming ~2.4GB total RAM (~60-100MB each) on a 30GB server. Process count grew from 6 to 42 over a single evening of usage. Root cause: SIGTERM not sent when session/subagent exits. Corroborated by #60656, #69145, #65694.

signals.topic: openclaw status/health CLI commands take 30-40 seconds per invocation due to jiti plugin normalization
signals.summary: CLI commands openclaw status and openclaw health take 40s and 17-42s respectively. Profiling confirms worker thread is pegged in jiti's normalizeAliases rebuilding the plugin graph from scratch for every CLI invocation rather than using a persistent filesystem cache.
signals.review_reason: CLI status and health commands take 30-40 seconds per invocation due to jiti rebuilding the plugin alias table for every CLI call. User time exceeds wall time confirms multi-threaded CPU bottleneck. This is a severe developer experience regression that makes routine monitoring commands practically unusable.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `openclaw status` / `openclaw health` take 40s / 17s — worker thread pegged in `jiti`'s `normalizeAliases`
source_issues.evidence: openclaw status takes 40.7s (62.8s CPU time), health takes 17-42s. V8 CPU profile shows worker isolate 61% JS, top hotspot is jiti normalizeAliases (16.8% ticks). Syscall profile rules out filesystem bottleneck. 161 plugins × ~27ms each. Version and help commands are fast (0.07-0.18s), confirming only cross-plugin commands are slow.

signals.topic: Agent retries full turns on terminal tool errors, causing duplicate messages to users
signals.summary: When tool calls fail with terminal errors (guildId required, node not connected), the agent runner retries the entire turn. Since the model generates text before the tool call, the text is delivered to the user on every retry. Users receive 7-10+ identical messages per interaction.
signals.review_reason: Terminal tool errors cause full turn retries without deduplication or max-turn limits, resulting in 7-10+ duplicate messages to users per interaction. Each retry also burns tokens/quota across all configured providers. This is a significant UX degradation and resource waste on every such tool failure.

source_issues.title: Message duplication: agent runner retries full turns on tool errors, resending text to user
source_issues.evidence: Terminal tool errors (guildId required, node not connected) trigger full turn retry without max-turn limit or abort. Each retry regenerates full assistant response (text + tool call), and text is delivered to user before tool executes and fails again. Results in 7-10+ identical messages per user input. Token quota burned on every retry.

signals.topic: Linux .deb package fails to install due to cross-device hard link error for icon file
signals.summary: The .deb package downloaded from the website fails to install on Linux with 'Invalid cross-device link' error when /tmp and /usr reside on different filesystems. This is a packaging build pipeline issue caused by electron-builder creating hard links that cannot survive dpkg's extraction to a tmpfs temp directory.
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine user-blocking installation failure on Linux. Users downloading the official .deb package from the website cannot install it when /tmp and /usr are on different filesystems (common on many Linux distros). The issue is well-documented with a clear root cause (electron-builder hard link + dpkg tmpfs extraction).

source_issues.title: .deb package fails to install: cross-device hard link error for icon file
source_issues.evidence: dpkg error: 'error creating hard link ./usr/share/icons/hicolor/1024x1024/apps/interpreter.png: Invalid cross-device link'. Root cause: electron-builder creates a hard link between icon files; dpkg extracts to tmpfs (/tmp) and cannot hard-link across filesystems to /usr.

signals.topic: Redteam composite/likert strategies always fail due to Cloudflare WAF blocking from high concurrency burst
signals.summary: The jailbreak:composite and jailbreak:likert redteam strategies consistently produce 0 test cases because 10 concurrent POST requests containing adversarial content trigger Cloudflare's WAF, which blocks the IP. The concurrency is hardcoded and cannot be reduced via CLI flags, making these strategies completely non-functional for all users. All other strategies succeed in the same run.
aliases: redteam composite likert cloudflare WAF block
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue for redteam users. The composite and likert strategies are completely non-functional — they always produce 0 test cases due to a hardcoded concurrency burst triggering Cloudflare WAF. Since the --max-concurrency flag does not affect these internal generators, there is no workaround. This directly blocks the redteam security testing workflow.

source_issues.title: jailbreak:composite and jailbreak:likert strategies always fail with Cloudflare WAF block
source_issues.evidence: Only 120 of 210 test cases generated. Composite and likert always produce 0. Root cause: 10 simultaneous POST requests containing adversarial content triggers Cloudflare WAF. No user-facing flag to reduce concurrency.

signals.topic: Credentials (API keys, Bearer tokens) leaked in plain text via UI Details panel and SQLite eval history
signals.summary: The promptfoo UI Details panel and ~/.promptfoo/promptfoo.db store provider configs verbatim, including rendered Authorization headers, API keys, and OAuth tokens. Users sharing debug info or with local machine access inadvertently expose live credentials. No masking exists for sensitive header fields (Authorization, X-Api-Key, Cookie) or config fields (apiKey, apiToken, authToken).
signals.review_reason: This is a credential leakage vulnerability with clear, direct user impact. Any user who copies the Details panel to share debug info — a common workflow — inadvertently exposes live API keys and bearer tokens in plain text. Additionally, the SQLite database stores every credential the user has ever evaluated against, accessible to anyone with machine access. This is a data exposure issue, not merely a security-related feature request.

source_issues.title: UI and stored eval record expose rendered Authorization / apiKey in plain text
source_issues.evidence: Credentials are persisted verbatim in SQLite ~/.promptfoo/promptfoo.db and displayed in the UI Details panel. Any user who shares debug info or has local machine access leaks all evaluated credentials.

signals.topic: Eval viewing crashes with RangeError for large evals (base64 images, large prompts) — results inaccessible via UI
signals.summary: The GET /eval/:id/table endpoint crashes with an unhandled RangeError when JSON.stringify() exceeds V8's ~512MB string limit. This happens with large evals containing base64-encoded images or large prompt content. The UI returns a 500 error and eval results are completely inaccessible.
aliases: eval table endpoint 500 crash large eval
RangeError JSON stringify V8 limit eval view
signals.review_reason: This blocks eval result viewing — a core post-eval workflow. When evals include base64 images or large outputs, the UI completely fails to load results with a 500 error. Users lose the ability to review their eval outputs through the primary interface.

source_issues.title: RangeError crash on GET /eval/:id/table for large evals
source_issues.evidence: Endpoint crashes with unhandled RangeError during JSON.stringify() for large eval payloads. The fix was addressed in PR #7599, indicating confirmed and acknowledged issue.

signals.topic: OpenRouter provider silently ignores user-supplied apiBaseUrl, always routing to hardcoded URL
signals.summary: The OpenRouterProvider hardcodes apiBaseUrl AFTER spreading user config, causing any user-supplied apiBaseUrl in promptfooconfig.yaml to be silently discarded. This blocks users who need to route through internal proxies (compliance gateways, caching layers) and causes silent failures via unexpected 401s from the proxy.
signals.review_reason: This is a silent misconfiguration bug — the user's intended proxy routing is completely ignored without any warning or error. Users who need enterprise proxy routing for OpenRouter are blocked. The silent nature (no error thrown) makes this especially problematic as users may not realize their traffic is going to the wrong endpoint.

source_issues.title: openrouter provider: hardcoded apiBaseUrl silently overrides user config
source_issues.evidence: Source code verified: hardcoded apiBaseUrl placed after user config spread, always wins. User-supplied value is silently dropped. Requests go to openrouter.ai regardless of user config.

signals.topic: Anthropic Opus 4.7+ temperature parameter causes 400 error — main eval flow blocked for newer models
signals.summary: As of Anthropic Opus 4.7, the temperature parameter is deprecated and causes a 400 error. The Anthropic provider explicitly sets temperature to 0 if undefined, so users cannot simply omit it. All eval runs against Opus 4.7+ models fail completely.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking issue for users on newer Anthropic Opus models. Every eval run fails with a 400 error because the provider unconditionally passes a now-deprecated parameter. There is no workaround without patching the source.

source_issues.title: Remove requirement for temperature parameter for anthropic models (at least)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed 400 error 'temperature is deprecated' when running against Opus 4.7. Provider hardcodes temperature=0 if undefined, so omission does not help.

signals.topic: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() 原地修改 ChatResponse.raw 导致调用方结构化响应对象被静默损坏
signals.summary: model_dump() 在序列化遥测数据时原地修改 self.response.raw，将 Pydantic 模型实例永久替换为 dict，导致所有访问 ChatResponse.raw 字段的代码抛出 AttributeError
aliases: StructuredLLM.achat returns dict instead of Pydantic model
signals.review_reason: 生产级阻断：StructuredLLM 是核心 API，在有遥测的生产环境中（OpenTelemetry 注册后），所有结构化输出完全损坏，错误向上传导导致整条规则集选择流程失败。log 证据显示真实业务逻辑（ruleset_selection）因 AttributeError 直接终止。P0 高频（影响所有 StructuredLLM + 遥测用户）+ 主流程阻断 + 有 log trace 支撑。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LLMChatEndEvent.model_dump() mutates ChatResponse.raw in-place, corrupting caller's response object
source_issues.evidence: 调用方使用 StructuredLLM.achat() 且启用 OpenTelemetry 时，ChatResponse.raw 从 Pydantic 模型实例变为 dict，后续所有访问 .answer 等字段的代码触发 AttributeError。生产环境启用遥测订阅时静默发生，日志显示 ruleset_selection 流程完全失败。

signals.topic: Bedrock nova-2-lite-v1:0 模型推理抛出 extraneous key textGenerationConfig 错误
signals.summary: 使用 global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 模型时，InvokeModel 调用因 textGenerationConfig 参数不被支持而报 ValidationException 异常
signals.review_reason: 明确的主流程失败：Bedrock 是官方集成，目标模型推理完全不可用，报 ValidationException 而非优雅降级。P0 降级原因：count=1，单仓问题，但有明确复现步骤和错误 trace。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Error with Bedrock's `global.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0`
source_issues.evidence: 直接复现：llama-index-llms-bedrock 在调用 nova-2-lite-v1:0 时抛出 botocore.errorfactory.ValidationException，提示 textGenerationConfig 为 extraneous key。其他 Bedrock 模型（如 claude-haiku）正常。

signals.topic: Anthropic LLM 配合 FunctionAgent 时 AgentStream.thinking_delta 完全缺失
signals.summary: Anthropic 流式输出时 thinking chunk 未被规范化到 ChatResponse.additional_kwargs，导致 workflow 层的 thinking_delta 为空，破坏思考过程可见性
aliases: Anthropic thinking blocks not forwarded to workflow
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：Anthropic thinking 是其核心竞争力特性，在 FunctionAgent workflow 中完全丢失。AgentStream.delta 和最终 response 正常（无崩溃），但 thinking_delta 对用户完全不可见，严重影响体验和调试能力。count=1 但影响明确，优先级 P1。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Missing AgentStream.thinking_delta when using Anthropic LLM with FunctionAgent
source_issues.evidence: 使用 streaming=True 的 FunctionAgent + Anthropic 模型时，AgentStream.delta 和最终响应正常，但 AgentStream.thinking_delta 全程为空，Anthropic thinking 内容对用户完全不可见。

signals.topic: Refine 综合器在 structured_answer_filtering=True 时忽略 query_satisfied=True，继续无效调用 LLM
signals.summary: 用户期望 Refine 在 query_satisfied=True 时提前终止，但实际对所有 chunk 都调用 LLM，造成 API 费用浪费和答案质量下降
aliases: Refine synthesizer ignores query_satisfied stop signal
signals.review_reason: 直接成本损失：structured_answer_filtering 的核心价值在于提前终止，但信号被忽略导致每次 query 都对所有 chunk 发起多余 LLM 调用，在大规模文档场景下浪费显著。count=1 但有清晰复现代码和成本证据。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Refine ignores `query_satisfied=True` when `structured_answer_filtering=True`
source_issues.evidence: 复现显示：单文档 query 应只需 1 次 LLM 调用，实际触发 3 次。query_satisfied=True 后仍然对每个 chunk 调用 LLM，浪费 API 费用。

signals.topic: Azure AI Search 向量存储将 falsy 值（0、空字符串、空列表）静默存储为 None，数据完整性损坏
signals.summary: metadata 中值为 0/''/[] 时被判断为 falsy 并存储为 None，检索时无法恢复原始值，造成静默数据损坏
aliases: falsy metadata stored as None azure aisearch
Azure AI Search silent data corruption metadata
signals.review_reason: 静默数据损坏：数值 0、空字符串、空列表等合法 falsy 值被无条件替换为 None，导致数据在检索后完全不可用，且无任何警告。影响 Azure AI Search 向量存储用户的核心数据完整性。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: falsy metadata values stored as None in Azure AI Search index
source_issues.evidence: metadata 值为整数 0 时，存取后变为 None。代码检查 'if metadata_value' 应改为 'if metadata_value is not None'。数值 0 被误判为无数据。

signals.topic: Windows daemon start/status crashes — `ps -o` incompatibility causes silent exit and false STOPPED reports
signals.summary: On Windows (Git Bash/msys2), `daemon start` silently exits within ~2s and `daemon status` always reports STOPPED because the `ps -o pid` Unix command is not supported. Both commands are rendered unusable, blocking the primary background-worker workflow for all Windows users.
aliases: daemon status false STOPPED on Windows
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports from different users on different Node versions confirm a primary workflow (background daemon) is completely broken on all Windows Git Bash/msys2 environments. Daemon start reports success but silently exits, making it a silent main-flow failure. Daemon status always lies. This blocks the core background worker pattern for the entire Windows user base.

source_issues.title: daemon start silently dies on Windows due to ps -o incompatibility
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed reproducer shows process exits within 2s, PID orphaned, daemon.log 0 bytes. Affects all Windows Git Bash users on both v3.5.7 and v3.5.80. Two independent project directories confirmed.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Daemon status shows STOPPED on Windows — ps -o pid command not supported
source_issues.evidence: ruflo daemon status reports STOPPED immediately after daemon start despite process running. ps: unknown option -- o error confirmed on Windows 11 Pro, Node v24.15.0, ruflo v3.5.80. Workaround requires cross-platform process.kill(pid,0) or platform-specific tasklist/ps.

signals.topic: Session save/list/crash — TypeError on save without swarm, corrupted list rows, session-end hang, undefined counters
signals.summary: Three session management commands are broken in v3.5.80: (a) session save throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined when no swarm is active; (b) session list renders corrupt rows with empty ID/name and 'Invalid Date' timestamps; (c) session-end hangs indefinitely leaving process orphaned. Corrupted entries accumulate with no valid ID to target for cleanup.
aliases: session save TypeError no active swarm
session list corrupted Invalid Date rows
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports covering four related session lifecycle bugs (save TypeError, list corruption, end hang, undefined counters). The session save TypeError is confirmed by both #1634 and #1626, indicating it's a consistent failure path. Session list corruption prevents users from managing their sessions at all. Session-end hang is a second hang variant beyond the post-task hang. The combination blocks the core end-of-session workflow.

source_issues.title: session save crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading agentCount)'; session list shows corrupt Invalid Date rows
source_issues.evidence: session save prints contradictory 'Session saved' then 'Failed to save session' with TypeError. session list shows ~10 rows with empty ID/name and 'Invalid Date In...' timestamps. session current reports 'No active session' immediately after save. No swarm initialized before save. Corrupted entries accumulate with no valid ID for session delete.

source_issues.title: CLI v3.5.80: session-end hang, session save TypeError, session list broken rendering
source_issues.evidence: session-end hangs at 0% CPU holding memory.db open after 'State saved to: .claude/sessions/...' is printed. session save throws same TypeError on 'agentCount' read. session list renders empty rows. Session summary shows 'undefined' for Tasks Succeeded/Failed. All four bugs reproduced in sequence during normal end-of-work wrap-up on a Next.js PR workflow with no special config.

signals.topic: ruflo hooks post-task hangs indefinitely after completing its work — CI scripts and slash commands stall
signals.summary: After `ruflo hooks post-task` records the outcome successfully (~1s), the Node process never exits, hanging until externally killed. All stdin variations tested hang, confirming a post-completion shutdown bug (unclosed timer/socket/Promise). Blocks CI scripts and slash command postflight blocks.
signals.review_reason: The hook records its outcome successfully but never exits, creating a hard block for any CI pipeline or slash command that calls it synchronously. The user had to wrap every invocation with `timeout 10` as a workaround. This is a clear workflow-blocking bug with documented real-world impact on slash command postflight execution.

source_issues.title: ruflo hooks post-task hangs indefinitely after recording outcome (v3.5.80)
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed hang with all stdin variations (empty stdin, echo, printf). Work completes in 1.1s but process hangs to timeout 60s. A /pdx-* slash command's Postflight block hung at 4m 53s before user intervention. Workaround requires wrapping every call with timeout 10. Root cause: unclosed handle (timer/socket/Promise) keeps Node event loop alive after outcome is recorded.

signals.topic: RvfBackend multi-writer silent data loss — 50-87.5% of concurrent writes silently dropped with no error signal
signals.summary: When multiple RvfBackend writers touch the same .rvf file, a snapshot-overwrite race and lock-starvation bug silently discards 50-87.5% of entries with zero error output. At N=2: 50% loss; N=4: 75%; N=8: 87.5% plus crashes. Affects multi-process CLI invocations, hook fan-out, swarm init, and multi-pane sessions.
aliases: snapshot overwrite race silent data loss
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss with no error signal is the most severe class of user pain. Callers get zero indication their data was dropped. The bug is 100% reproducible, confirmed deterministic across 20 trials, and verified fixed by a patch. The signature 'exactly 1/N entries survive' proves last-writer's stale snapshot overwrites all peer writes. Any multi-process or concurrent workflow touching RvfBackend loses data silently.

source_issues.title: RvfBackend: multi-writer silently loses data (snapshot-overwrite race + lock starvation) — fix included
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible across 20 trials per scenario with in-process harness (ruled out cold-start/SIGTERM confounds). At N=2: 50% loss, N=4: 75%, N=8: 87.5% loss + all writers crash. Zero errors, zero crashes at low N — just missing data. Fix (132-line patch) verified: 0% loss at all N after patch. Root cause: stale in-memory snapshot overwrites peer writes at shutdown, and acquireLock() has only ~500ms retry budget insufficient for N=8 contention.

signals.topic: hooks pretrain and neural train are silently broken — no-op on Windows, zero loss reported, no data persisted
signals.summary: Both the pretrain and neural train learning surfaces are silently broken on v3.5.41+: pretrain prints success but writes zero bytes to any target (patterns.json unchanged by MD5 diff); neural train reports 'Avg Loss 0.0000, Delta Norm 0.000000' every epoch (optimizer dead). Users cannot distinguish inert output from successful operation without MD5-diffing files themselves.
aliases: neural train optimizer dead zero loss
signals.review_reason: Two core advertised learning features are completely inert (no-op + zero gradient), yet both print success strings. This is a deceptive silent failure: users believe their intelligence bootstrapping is working when nothing is being learned or persisted. The memory store/search pipeline (which actually works) is undocumented as the fallback path. The MD5-diff evidence is objective and unambiguous.

source_issues.title: hooks pretrain is a no-op and neural train optimizer is dead on v3.5.41 (Windows)
source_issues.evidence: MD5 of patterns.json identical before and after pretrain run. 1.0s wall-time implausible for a 4-step RETRIEVE/JUDGE/DISTILL/CONSOLIDATE pipeline. Neural train writes cwd-scoped patterns.json (not global path) containing action pattern list, not learned weights. Users wrote multi-hundred-line 'system is inert' internal reports before discovering memory store/search was doing real work. Only workaround is to use memory store/search directly, bypassing the advertised learning surfaces.

signals.topic: Windows Git Bash: `open <url>` hangs indefinitely, blocking the main workflow
signals.summary: On Windows 11 with Git Bash, `agent-browser --session <name> open <url>` hangs indefinitely with no stdout or error. The CLI never returns even after fresh OS reboot and with no stale PID/port files. Users building verification layers have their entire automation gate stall because `open` never completes.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow command (`open`) completely blocks on Windows Git Bash with no error output. The user's automation pipeline cannot proceed. Reproduced with fresh state and multiple attempts. High user impact: entire verification gate stalls.

source_issues.title: open <url> hangs indefinitely on Windows Git Bash (post-reboot + clean pid files, no Chromium zombies)
source_issues.evidence: Main command `agent-browser open <url>` hangs indefinitely with no output or error on Windows Git Bash, even after fresh OS reboot. Full verification gate stalls.

signals.topic: CDP connection silently fails when external Chrome restarts — no URL rediscovery
signals.summary: When connecting via `agent-browser connect ws://localhost:9222`, if Chrome is closed and restarted, Chrome generates a new webSocketDebuggerUrl UUID. The agent-browser daemon skips reconnection when already running and continues using the stale UUID, causing the connection to silently fail with a misleading error message.
signals.review_reason: CDP connection silently fails when Chrome restarts. The daemon holds a stale connection URL and skips reconnection. Root cause in source code identified. Causes repeated workflow failures for external Chrome users.

source_issues.title: CDP connection fails silently when external browser restarts (new webSocketDebuggerUrl)
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in cli/src/main.rs: daemon skips reconnect when already running. Chrome generates new webSocketDebuggerUrl UUID on restart, daemon uses stale URL, connection silently fails with misleading error.

signals.topic: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG regression: Chrome killed after 7–9 seconds idle in multi-threaded runtime
signals.summary: v0.24.1 introduced PR_SET_PDEATHSIG which tracks the spawning thread rather than process. Tokio recycles the worker thread after idle time, triggering SIGKILL to Chrome even though the daemon is still alive. All pages go to about:blank after ~7 seconds, breaking downloads and any automation longer than 7 seconds.
signals.review_reason: Regression that kills Chrome after 7-9 seconds of idle time on every site. Breaks downloads (first works, second fails) and any workflow exceeding 7 seconds between commands. Root cause identified in tokio multi-threaded runtime.

source_issues.title: fix: PR_SET_PDEATHSIG kills Chrome in tokio multi-threaded runtime (v0.24.1 regression)
source_issues.evidence: Chrome killed after ~7-9 seconds idle on every page every site. Root cause: tokio worker thread recycling triggers PR_SET_PDEATHSIG. All pages navigate to about:blank. Downloads broken. Automation >7s between commands fails.

signals.topic: macOS: Chrome orphan persists after network blip, degrading main Chrome throughput 17x
signals.summary: On macOS with agent-browser v0.26.0, a brief network drop during an active session causes the spawned Chrome to become an orphan that persists indefinitely. The orphan holds the remote-debugging-port open and shared profile state, causing the user's normal Chrome throughput to degrade from 700+ Mbps to 36 Mbps (17x reduction) until the orphan is manually killed.
aliases: Chrome process not killed on CDP failure
signals.review_reason: Network blip causes Chrome orphan that persists 24+ hours and degrades the user's primary Chrome profile throughput by 17x. Clear cost: user loses 95% of normal browsing speed until orphan is manually killed. Regression from v0.25.2 fix for another issue.

source_issues.title: Chrome orphan after network blip during --profile / cookie-bypass sessions on macOS (v0.26.0, regression counterpart to #1157)
source_issues.evidence: Network blip during session causes Chrome to become orphan. User's normal Chrome degraded from 700+ Mbps to 36 Mbps (17x). Regression from v0.25.2 where PR_SET_PDEATHSIG was removed. Chrome process persists 24+ hours with temp profile dirs.

signals.topic: Semantic locators cannot find elements inside Shadow DOM, blocking Web Component automation
signals.summary: Semantic locators like `find placeholder Password fill testpass` return 'Element not found' when the target element is inside a Shadow DOM. This blocks automation of Web Components, a widespread pattern in modern web development (Google products, Microsoft Fluent, etc.).
signals.review_reason: Semantic locators fail for Shadow DOM elements, which are a standard web platform feature used in Google, Microsoft, and many other major web frameworks. This blocks a significant class of modern web app automation.

source_issues.title: Semantic locators do not work throw shadow dom
source_issues.evidence: Semantic locator command `find placeholder Password fill` fails with 'Element not found' for elements inside Shadow DOM. Blocks Web Component automation.

signals.topic: Chatbot returns 'Oops, an error occurred!' on every user message, blocking main conversational flow
signals.summary: 用户每次发送消息时，聊天机器人均返回泛化错误消息 'Oops, an error occurred!'，导致对话主流程完全不可用，用户无法正常使用聊天功能。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1 频次较低，但该问题属于主流程阻断级别：用户在聊天主交互路径上每次操作都遇到泛化错误，核心功能完全不可用。题目明确、时间极新（2026-04-20），且错误消息为 'Oops, an error occurred!' 这种对用户完全无诊断信息的泛化提示，属于典型阻断性用户体验问题，因此保留为 pain point。但因 count=1 且仅单仓，P2 更为合理。

source_issues.title: Well it doesn't work it always says : Oops, an error occurred!
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告聊天机器人每次发消息都显示 'Oops, an error occurred!'，附截图；无评论说明问题未得到解决；状态仍为 open，主流程完全阻断。

signals.topic: embed/embedMany runtime crash with EmbeddingModelV2 providers due to undefined warnings
signals.summary: When using any EmbeddingModelV2-based provider (e.g. @ai-sdk/google-vertex@3.x), embed() and embedMany() crash at runtime with TypeError because doEmbed does not return a `warnings` property but the SDK assumes it is always present and iterable. Affects two code paths: logWarnings() and embed-many.ts spread operator.
signals.review_reason: Runtime crash (TypeError) in core embedding APIs when using EmbeddingModelV2 providers. Two separate code paths fail: logWarnings() and the embedMany spread operator. This blocks the primary embedding use case for any v2-based provider including google-vertex.

source_issues.title: embed/embedMany crash: 'warnings' is undefined from EmbeddingModelV2 providers
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length') at logWarnings in embed.ts:180 AND TypeError: result.warnings is not iterable at embed-many.ts:312. Affects ai@6.0.149 through at least ai@6.0.158 with any EmbeddingModelV2 provider.

signals.topic: AI Gateway throws misleading error when listing available models due to missing 'reranking' modelType in hardcoded Zod enum
signals.summary: gateway.getAvailableModels() throws a GatewayResponseError with misleading message 'Invalid error response format' because the SDK's hardcoded Zod enum in gateway-fetch-metadata.ts is missing the 'reranking' modelType that the live Gateway now serves. The validation failure then cascades into a misleading error message. Recurring bug — same class as #12732 for the 'video' modelType.
signals.review_reason: gateway.getAvailableModels() completely breaks — throws an exception instead of returning the model list. The error message is misleading ('Invalid error response format') masking the real cause (missing enum value), making debugging difficult. Same class of bug recurred after #12732 which added 'video'.

source_issues.title: gateway.getAvailableModels() throws on cohere/rerank-v3.5: schema enum missing 'reranking'
source_issues.evidence: gateway.getAvailableModels() throws: GatewayResponseError: Invalid error response format: Gateway request failed → APICallError: Invalid JSON response → AI_TypeValidationError on path ['models', 69, 'modelType'] → ZodError: Invalid option: expected one of 'embedding'|'image'|'language'|'video'. Confirmed live with cohere/rerank-v3.5 as of 2026-04-14.

signals.topic: MCP HTTP/SSE transport does not downgrade mcp-protocol-version header after version negotiation, violating MCP spec and blocking servers like Figma Dev Mode
signals.summary: HttpMCPTransport and SseMCPTransport always emit LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION in the mcp-protocol-version header after initialization instead of the negotiated version returned by the server. This violates the MCP spec and causes post-initialization requests to fail (400 Bad Request) against any MCP server that does not support the latest protocol version, including Figma Dev Mode MCP Server.
aliases: MCP protocol version not downgraded after negotiate
MCP transport spec violation blocking servers
signals.review_reason: Critical MCP connectivity bug: the SDK fails spec compliance and breaks the entire MCP client workflow against real-world servers (Figma Dev Mode) that support older protocol versions. The client never connects — every post-init request gets 400. Blocking real production use of @ai-sdk/mcp with common MCP servers.

source_issues.title: [@ai-sdk/mcp] Streamable HTTP transport does not downgrade mcp-protocol-version header after version negotiation (breaks servers like Figma Dev Mode MCP)
source_issues.evidence: createMCPClient() against Figma Dev Mode MCP never resolves — notifications/initialized returns 400: 'Unsupported protocol version (supported versions: 2025-06-18...)'. Server negotiates 2025-06-18 but client keeps sending 2025-11-25 in header. Affects @ai-sdk/mcp 1.0.36 and 2.0.0-beta.25.

signals.topic: Google provider sends $ref/$defs JSON Schema in function response content, causing Gemini API 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT errors
signals.summary: When a tool's execute() returns a raw JS object containing JSON Schema $ref/$defs (e.g. from Zod v4's z.toJSONSchema() with z.lazy()), the Google provider sends it directly to Gemini without sanitization. Gemini interprets the $ref pointers and rejects with 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT, blocking the entire multi-step tool execution pipeline.
aliases: Gemini rejects JSON Schema $ref in function responses
Google provider 400 on $defs in tool result
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocked: tool execution with Google provider fails with 400 API error when tool results contain JSON Schema $ref/$defs. This is a common pattern with Zod v4's z.lazy() for recursive schemas. Every multi-step tool call using recursive schemas against Gemini fails.

source_issues.title: Gemini rejects `$ref`/`$defs` in function response content (400 INVALID_ARGUMENT)
source_issues.evidence: Gemini returns HTTP 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT: 'The referenced name `#/$defs/__schema0` in function_response.response does not match a display_name'. Full reproduction provided with Zod v4 z.lazy() schema causing z.toJSONSchema() to emit $ref/$defs. Blocks streamText with multi-step tool calls using recursive schemas.

signals.topic: AI Gateway silently ignores mask parameter for OpenAI inpainting (gpt-image-1) and generates entirely new image
signals.summary: When using generateImage() with @ai-sdk/gateway and providing a mask parameter for OpenAI inpainting (gpt-image-1), the Gateway silently ignores the mask and generates a completely new image instead of editing only the masked region. No error or warning is returned. The Gateway routes to /v1/images/generations instead of /v1/images/edits.
aliases: Gateway mask parameter silently dropped for image inpainting
signals.review_reason: Critical silent data corruption in image editing workflow: the mask parameter is completely ignored and an entirely new image is generated with no warning. The user gets wrong output with no indication of failure. This is worse than a hard error because the operation appears to succeed. Affects a key image editing use case (inpainting) via the Gateway.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway silently ignores mask parameter for OpenAI inpainting (gpt-image-1)
source_issues.evidence: Mask completely ignored — entire image regenerated from scratch with no warnings or errors. Same image+mask+prompt sent directly to OpenAI /v1/images/edits produces correct inpainting (only masked area regenerated). Server logs confirm mask reaches generateImage() but Gateway routes to wrong endpoint. Affects ai@6.0.158, @ai-sdk/gateway@3.0.95.

signals.topic: Build crash during prerender of _global-error in Next.js 16 (isPageStatic hardcodes route, ignoring dynamic export)
signals.summary: Three issues (93011, 93024, 93012) report that build crashes during prerender of /_global-error in Next.js 16 with TypeError (cannot read properties of null reading 'useContext'). The isPageStatic() function hardcodes _global-error route ignoring dynamic export config.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker — fresh Next.js 16 scaffold cannot complete build. Affects both webpack and Turbopack. Users must pin canary to get a working build, blocking new project setup and CI/CD pipelines. 3 independent reports with clear reproduction steps on create-next-app scaffold.

source_issues.title: Next 16.2.4: next build crashes prerendering /_global-error with TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useContext')
source_issues.evidence: Build fails with TypeError during prerender of /_global-error. Works on 16.3.0-canary.2. Affects fresh create-next-app scaffolds.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16: isPageStatic() hardcodes _global-error as isStatic with empty appConfig, causing prerender crash when root layout uses React context
source_issues.evidence: isPageStatic() hardcodes _global-error route with appConfig: {}. export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic' is ignored. Crashes during prerender when root layout uses React context.

source_issues.title: next build fails on Node 25 during prerender (Next 15 and 16 scaffolds)
source_issues.evidence: Build fails on Node 25 during prerender of /_global-error (16) or /404 (15). Works on Node 20. Pristine create-next-app scaffold affected.

signals.topic: Memory leak in Next.js 16.x stable causing production OOM crashes — fixes exist in canary but not backported for 45+ days
signals.summary: Two issues (93069, 93068) report a memory leak in Next.js 16.x stable causing repeated production OOM kills. Fixes are confirmed in canary (PRs #88577, #89040) but have not been backported to stable for 45+ days.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker — production services OOM and get killed repeatedly every 8 hours. Clear cost loss (repeated service restarts, failed deployments on Render). Fix exists in canary but not backported for 45+ days despite multiple requests. Real production data showing 4 OOM kills in 7 days.

source_issues.title: Memory leak fix from canary (PRs #88577, #89040) still not in any 16.x stable release 45+ days later — production OOMs ongoing on 16.2.4
source_issues.evidence: Production OOM kills every 8 hours on Render 512MiB instance. Memory climbs ~30 MiB/hour at 0% CPU. 4 confirmed oomKilled events in 7 days. Fixes exist in canary (16.3.0-canary.2) but 16.x stable releases continue to ship without them.

source_issues.title: Memory leak fix from canary (PRs #88577, #89040) still not in any 16.x stable release 45+ days later — production OOMs ongoing on 16.2.4
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of 93069. Same production OOM evidence with WriteWrap._chunks retainer chain and Render oomKilled events.

signals.topic: Turbopack RAM exhaustion (40+ GB) and infinite worker spawn loop from misdetected workspace root due to orphan parent lockfile
signals.summary: Two issues (92978, 92977) report that Turbopack misdetects workspace root when an orphan package-lock.json exists in the parent directory (common on Windows), causing unbounded RAM growth to 40+ GB, infinite module resolution retry, and machine freeze.
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocker — dev server becomes completely unusable causing machine freeze/OOM. Worker processes spawn infinitely without bound consuming 40+ GB RAM. Affects Windows users where orphan lockfiles in home directory are common. Machine becomes unresponsive requiring hard restart.

source_issues.title: Turbopack: misdetected workspace root (from stray parent lockfile) causes RAM exhaustion (40+ GB) and infinite module-resolution retry on first request
source_issues.evidence: RAM grows to 43,516 MB with 20+ child workers. Machine becomes unresponsive. Orphan package-lock.json in home directory causes wrong workspace root inference, leading to file watcher scanning tens of GB of user files.

source_issues.title: misdetected workspace root (from stray parent lockfile) causes RAM exhaustion (40+ GB) and infinite module-resolution retry on first request
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of 92978. Same RAM exhaustion and workspace misdetection issue.

signals.topic: next/image in dev mode shows stale image after file edit when filename is unchanged
signals.summary: Two issues (93075, 93072) report that next/image in dev mode caches local images by filename only, showing stale versions after file edits until the user renames the file or deletes .next cache.
signals.review_reason: Developer UX issue — requires workaround (rename file or clear .next) to see image updates. Does not block main flow but degrades development iteration speed for image-heavy apps. 2 independent reports with clear reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: next/image in dev does not update local image after file edit with same filename
source_issues.evidence: next/image shows old cached version while plain img updates correctly. Workaround requires renaming file or deleting .next cache. Affects local development workflow.

source_issues.title: next/image in dev can keep showing stale local image after editing same file until .next is deleted and dev server restarted
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of 93075. Same stale image caching issue in dev mode.

signals.topic: Router state header parse error during version skew (v15 prefetching to v16 server) causing 500 errors
signals.summary: Issue 92961 reports that during v15 to v16 rolling deployment, v15 pages prefetching links to the v16 server receive 'router state header could not be parsed' errors with 500 responses.
signals.review_reason: Blocks v15 to v16 migration for apps using dynamic APIs in not-found.tsx. Prefetch requests fail with 500 during rolling deployments, causing broken navigation for end users. Multiple confirmed users on social media provide social proof of impact.

source_issues.title: The router state header was sent but could not be parsed error occurs during version skew (v15 => v16.2)
source_issues.evidence: Error occurs when v15 page prefetches links to v16 server. Prefetch returns 500. Affects deployments during version migration. Multiple users confirming on social media.

signals.topic: getProjects API response breaks Zod schema validation after SDK upgrade
signals.summary: 用户升级 SDK 到 1.18.9 后，getProjects 返回的响应无法通过 Zod schema 校验。API 返回的字段（如 alias、security）与 SDK 定义的类型不匹配，导致整个项目列表查询主流程阻断。
aliases: getProjects response schema mismatch after upgrade
signals.review_reason: getProjects 是 SDK 最核心的 API 之一，其响应校验失败直接导致调用方无法获取项目列表，构成主流程阻断。虽然仅 1 条 issue，但错误信息详尽（覆盖 45+ 个项目对象的 alias 字段报错 + security 字段联合类型不匹配），反映了 API schema 与 SDK 类型定义之间的系统性不一致，是需要修复的真实用户痛点。

source_issues.title: `getProjects` response validation error
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告从 SDK 1.18.7 升级到 1.18.9 后，getProjects 返回大量 ZodError，错误涉及 projects[].alias 期望 array 但收到 undefined，以及 projects[].security 字段结构不匹配（如期望 undefined/null/object 但实际结构缺少子字段 managedRules.vercel_ruleset 等）。用户明确表示 'I upgraded from SDK 1.18.7 to 1.18.9 this morning' 且报错阻断主流程。

signals.topic: Yarn 4 `catalog:` protocol 导致 `turbo query affectedPackages` 误报未变更 workspace 为受影响
signals.summary: 当 root package.json 使用 Yarn 4 的 `catalog:` 协议时，`turbo query affectedPackages` 对所有未变更的 workspace 报告 `LockfileChanged { added: [], removed: [] }`，导致 CI 过滤逻辑失效、下游流水线误触发。
aliases: Yarn 4 catalog protocol lockfile false positive
affectedPackages LockfileChanged empty deltas with catalog
signals.review_reason: P0: `affectedPackages`返回空delta是主流程阻断性问题——导致CI/CD管道无法正确判断哪些workspace需重新构建，在大规模monorepo(110+ workspaces)中会强制全量构建，造成显著CI时间/成本浪费。有明确根因定位(yarnrc=None导致catalog解析不对称)和完整复现步骤。

source_issues.title: `turbo query affectedPackages` reports empty `LockfileChanged` deltas when root package.json uses Yarn 4 `catalog:` protocol
source_issues.evidence: 影响CI流水线：issue明确描述生产monorepo(~110 workspaces)采纳catalog后，100%的LockfileChanged条目变为空delta，导致下游CI过滤逻辑(added==0 && removed==0)完全失效，所有lockfile提交都触发全量构建。同时在控制分支实验中，pkg-b未被修改却被报告为affected，产生幽灵依赖条目。

signals.topic: Turborepo AI Skill 的命令调度器绝对禁止 Root Task 与 SKILL.md 矛盾，生成错误配置指导
signals.summary: Turborepo skill 的 command/turborepo.md 包含绝对规则'DO NOT create Root Tasks'，与 SKILL.md 中'Root Tasks仅用于真正无法存在于packages的任务'的描述矛盾，导致AI agent对Vitest Projects等合法根任务场景生成错误指引。
aliases: turborepo skill rejects valid root tasks
Skill与文档矛盾导致AI生成错误配置
signals.review_reason: P1: Skill生成错误配置指导影响AI辅助编码的主流程，虽非turbo runtime崩溃但会阻断用户依赖AI skill正确配置monorepo的场景（Vitest Projects、release script等合法根任务被拒绝），且已在客户生产monorepo中被触发发现。count=1单仓问题不满足P0条件。

source_issues.title: Turborepo skill: command dispatcher contradicts SKILL.md on Root Tasks
source_issues.evidence: Skill dispatcher在用户调用/turborepo时作为权威行为源，绝对规则导致agent拒绝正确配置（如Vitest Projects的//#test、changeset发布、repo级别linter等合法场景）。在客户monorepo的PR中被发现并标记为上游问题，需在上游修复而非本地补丁。

signals.topic: Vercel Toolbar iframe blocked by COEP/CORP policy mismatch, breaking toolbar rendering in COEP-strict apps
signals.summary: The Vercel Toolbar iframe loaded from vercel.live fails to render when the host app uses Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy (COEP), because the embedded resources lack the Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header. This forces users to downgrade COEP to unsafe-none, sacrificing browser isolation guarantees just to use the toolbar.
signals.review_reason: Toolbar is a core developer experience feature. Its complete failure to render in COEP-strict environments (the recommended posture per Chrome's Spectre mitigation guidance) directly blocks a main workflow. Users must sacrifice browser security isolation just to use the toolbar, which is a significant user impact.

source_issues.title: @vercel/toolbar iframe from vercel.live missing CORP header, fails to embed under COEP=credentialless
source_issues.evidence: Toolbar does not appear on COEP-strict apps. Browser console shows iframe blocked by COEP, assigned chrome-error:// pseudo-origin, breaking postMessage handshake. Workaround requires dropping COEP to unsafe-none.

signals.topic: Python local dev with `vercel dev` broken when uv >= 0.10.11 is installed
signals.summary: getDevPythonVersion() hardcodes Python minor version to 0 (3.0), which newer uv versions reject as unsupported. This breaks all Python serverless function development locally for any user with uv >= 0.10.11, returning HTTP 500 on every Python API call.
signals.review_reason: Local dev for Python serverless functions is a primary development workflow. The bug causes all Python function calls to fail with HTTP 500, which is a complete workflow blockage. The root cause is clear (hardcoded Python 3.0) and affects any user with a modern uv installation.

source_issues.title: getDevPythonVersion() hardcodes minor: 0, breaks local dev with uv >= 0.10.11
source_issues.evidence: vercel dev calls 'uv venv --python 3.0', which uv 0.10.11 explicitly rejects with 'Python <3.7 is not supported but 3.0 was requested'. Every API call to a Python function returns HTTP 500. Older uv accepted 3.0 as 'any Python 3'.

signals.topic: CLI `vc link` incorrectly links to wrong project, causing deployments to target wrong project and use wrong OIDC token
signals.summary: When multiple Vercel projects have similar names (e.g., 'covillage-portal' and 'covillage'), `vc link` correctly identifies and stores the right project in .vercel/project.json but downloads environment variables from and deploys to the wrong project, silently using a mismatched OIDC token.
aliases: vercel link deploys to wrong project
signals.review_reason: A silent cross-project credential mismatch is a high-impact issue. The user gets no error but deploys to the wrong project with the wrong OIDC token, which could lead to secrets being written to the wrong project. This is a workflow-runtime failure with significant potential for data confusion or exposure.

source_issues.title: CLI: I can't deploy because `vc link` keeps linking wrong project
source_issues.evidence: vc link successfully writes correct project name and ID to .vercel/project.json but downloads env vars from wrong project and updates VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN to the wrong project's token. User ends up deploying to wrong project with mismatched credentials.

signals.topic: Environment variable values silently accept trailing whitespace/newlines from piped input, causing silent API key failures
signals.summary: Using `vercel env add` with piped input (e.g., echo) silently stores trailing newlines in environment variable values. This causes API keys and tokens to appear correct but be functionally invalid, leading to frustrating debugging sessions with no error message.
aliases: env variable value trailing newline silent failure
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption in credentials is a genuine user pain point causing significant debugging time. While only one report, the root cause (stdin piping behavior) is a common pattern that likely affects multiple users who don't notice until production failures occur.

source_issues.title: `vercel env add` should warn or strip trailing whitespace/newlines from values
source_issues.evidence: echo 'my-api-key' | vercel env add MY_VAR production stores 'my-api-key\n' instead of 'my-api-key'. The API key appears correct but is silently invalid. User describes 'frustrating debugging session' with no indication of the root cause.

signals.topic: Vercel CLI packages include outdated dependencies with known security vulnerabilities (path-to-regexp, undici, esbuild)
signals.summary: The Vercel CLI transitively pulls packages with known security vulnerabilities (path-to-regexp, undici, esbuild) for which patches are available but not applied. This causes CI/CD pipelines with audit requirements to fail or require expensive exemptions.
aliases: npm audit fails for Vercel CLI
signals.review_reason: Supply chain vulnerabilities in the CLI tool affect all users running audits in automated pipelines. While the vulnerabilities are not confirmed exploitable in Vercel's context, the CI failures and policy exemption costs represent a real operational burden for enterprise users.

source_issues.title: Latest version of cli is pulling in insecure packages that have available patches
source_issues.evidence: CLI pulls path-to-regexp, undici, esbuild with known vulnerabilities. 'npm audit' fails in CI for security policy compliance. User states 'security policies can make these expensive to ignore'. Multiple linked PRs show Vercel is aware but fixes have been reverted or not released.

signals.topic: Claude Agent / model selection fails to launch in multiple scenarios (ACP variant mismatch, devEngines conflict)
signals.summary: Claude Agent in Zed is completely inaccessible due to two distinct failure modes: (1) ACP returns an unknown `ClaudeAgent` variant causing deserialization failure at startup, and (2) npm EBADDEVENGINES error when a project has a package.json with devEngines.packageManager set to pnpm. Both scenarios result in the AI agent being unusable, blocking a core Zed feature.
aliases: Claude Opus 4.6 disappeared from Zed Agent
signals.review_reason: Three separate issues all result in Claude Agent being completely inaccessible, which is a primary Zed feature. Issue #54327 shows a deserialization error at startup (error log provided); #54323 shows npm EBADDEVENGINES preventing ACP from running; #54351 shows model versions missing from the selector. All have clear error logs and user-visible blocking behavior.

source_issues.title: Claude Agent inaccessible
source_issues.evidence: Agent panel replaced with generic LLM panel on startup. Error log: unknown variant `ClaudeAgent`, expected one of `NativeAgent`, `TextThread`...

source_issues.title: Claude-ACP fails with devEngines in project package.json
source_issues.evidence: npm EBADDEVENGINES error blocks Claude ACP from launching in projects with devEngines.packageManager set. Full npm error log with EBADDEVENGINES code.

source_issues.title: Claude Opus 4.6 & 4.5 disappeared from Zed Agent's Github Copilot ACP in v0.232.3
source_issues.evidence: Claude Opus 4.6 and 4.5 no longer appear in model selector dropdown for GitHub Copilot ACP. Key AI model versions made unavailable.

signals.topic: Recent projects panel UI: button overflow and shortcut label misalignment across multiple menus
signals.summary: The recent projects panel and related menus display two consistent UI issues: (1) buttons overflow their container when users have long keybind combinations, and (2) shortcut labels are not vertically aligned to a shared right-side column in various menus (workspace switcher, quick-switch, recent projects). These are visual papercut issues affecting the UI polish.
signals.review_reason: Three issues from the same reporter across multiple menus (recent projects, workspace switcher) all describe shortcut/button label misalignment and overflow. These are consistent papercut UI issues. count=3 meets the threshold. P2 fits as these are visual polish issues — they do not block editing, linting, AI features, or any core workflow.

source_issues.title: Overflowing buttons in recent project panel
source_issues.evidence: Button UI overflows with long keybind combinations. User provided screenshot showing visual overflow in the button bar.

source_issues.title: Bug: Shortcut labels are not aligned in recent projects quick-switch menu
source_issues.evidence: Shortcut labels appear at inconsistent horizontal positions across rows in the recent projects quick-switch menu. Screenshots provided showing misalignment.

source_issues.title: Shortcut text misaligned in workspace switcher menu
source_issues.evidence: Shortcut text in workspace switcher dropdown not aligned to a shared right-side column. Two rows have visibly different horizontal positions for shortcut text. Screenshots provided.

signals.topic: Project search Replace All hangs in infinite loop when search text contains `##` markdown heading prefix
signals.summary: Using Ctrl+Alt+Enter (replace all) in project search causes an infinite loop and indefinite GUI blinking when the search or replace text contains `##` followed by non-ASCII characters. The replacement repeats indefinitely until the user manually closes the project search window. This is a complete workflow blocker for users working with markdown files.
aliases: Replace all infinite loop markdown heading
Project search replace hangs with ## prefix
signals.review_reason: While count=1, the infinite loop behavior is a severe workflow blocker that corrupts file state and forces manual intervention. The evidence includes a YouTube video showing the repeating replacement and explicit description of the indefinite loop. This warrants P1 despite single-instance due to severity.

source_issues.title: Project search: Replace all hangs in infinite loop when search/replace text shares a common prefix with `##`
source_issues.evidence: GUI starts blinking and repeats replacement indefinitely when replacing markdown heading text. Issue persists until user closes project search window. Reproduced with Japanese markdown headings (## この日に作成したノート).

signals.topic: JetBrains keymap: single Shift press closes panels unexpectedly due to Shift-Shift global bind
signals.summary: On the JetBrains base keymap, pressing the Shift key once (without a second press) causes panels to close unexpectedly. The Shift-Shift keybind cannot be disabled, meaning users cannot use the Shift key in normal editing without triggering panel dismissal. This disrupts editing workflow for JetBrains keymap users.
aliases: Shift key closes panel JetBrains keymap
signals.review_reason: The issue blocks normal text editing on the JetBrains keymap since Shift is frequently used. Labeled 'state:reproducible' by Zed team. Though frequency is 'uncommon', the UX impact is significant — every Shift press in editing unintentionally closes panels. P1 fits better than P2 as it directly blocks core editing workflow.

source_issues.title: Shift Closes Panels on Jetbrains base keymap
source_issues.evidence: Pressing Shift once on JetBrains keymap closes the panel. Shift-Shift global keybind cannot be disabled. Marked as state:reproducible by maintainers.

signals.topic: ESLint language server fails to start when Zed opens a nested subdirectory workspace
signals.summary: ESLint fails to start with 'The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect (os error 123)' when Zed opens a project folder containing a subdirectory as workspace (e.g., opening agents-party/src/agentsparty/frontend). ESLint only works when the frontend folder is opened as the sole workspace root. This is a key linting feature failure in multi-project monorepo setups.
aliases: ESLint fails in nested subdirectory workspace
signals.review_reason: ESLint failure in monorepo/nested workspace scenarios blocks a critical development feature (linting). Has clear error log evidence (os error 123) and a workaround exists (open subdirectory alone), but this is a significant DX issue for monorepo users. P1 fits as it affects a core dev feature in common project structures.

source_issues.title: ESLint fails to start.
source_issues.evidence: ESLint server fails with 'The filename, directory name, or volume label syntax is incorrect (os error 123)'. Works when opening frontend folder alone but fails when opening parent workspace. Error log shows: Failed to start language server 'eslint'.
